tr: a. 牢固的, 根深蒂固的

s. established firmly and securely

tr: n. 企業家, 主辦人
[經] 承包商, 企業家
創業者；企業家
def: n. someone who organizes a business venture and assumes the risk for it
someone who starts a business and takes financial risks

ex.en: The young entrepreneur opened a bakery near our station.
ex.zh: 那位年輕創業者在我們車站附近開了一家麵包店。

ex.en: Local governments can support entrepreneurs by simplifying regulations and improving access to affordable loans.
ex.zh: 地方政府可以通過簡化規定、便利獲取低息貸款來支持創業者。

col: a successful entrepreneur｜成功的企業家
words.tip: 強調創辦企業並承擔風險，不泛指經理。

tr: vt. 信託, 交託, 委託
[經] 委託
委託；託付
def: v. confer a trust upon
v. put into the care or protection of someone
To give someone responsibility for something or someone valuable.

ex.en: I entrusted my neighbour with the spare house key.
ex.zh: 我把家裡的備用鑰匙託付給了鄰居。

ex.en: Parents entrust schools with their children's education and expect teachers to provide a safe learning environment.
ex.zh: 家長把孩子的教育託付給學校，並期待教師提供安全的學習環境。

col: entrust someone with a task｜委託某人執行任務
entrust something to someone｜把某物託付給某人
entrust someone with responsibility｜委以某人重任
words.tip: entrust人with物；entrust物to人。

tr: v. (使)纏住, (使)盤繞, (使)糾纏

[法] 舉出, 列舉, 枚舉
列舉；逐一列出
def: v. specify individually
To name things separately, one after another.

ex.en: She enumerated the repairs needed before we could move in.
ex.zh: 她逐一列出了我們入住前需要完成的維修項目。

ex.en: The report enumerates several barriers to higher education, including tuition costs and limited access to reliable transport.
ex.zh: 該報告列舉了接受高等教育的幾項障礙，包括學費和缺乏可靠的交通服務。

col: enumerate the reasons｜逐一列出原因
enumerate the main points｜逐一列出要點
words.tip: 正式用詞，強調逐項列出；日常表達常用list。

def: v extend on all sides of simultaneously; encircle

設想；展望
def: v form a mental image of something that is not present or that is not the case
To imagine a possible future situation or event.

ex.en: I envisage turning this spare room into a studio.
ex.zh: 我設想把這間空房改成工作室。

ex.en: Urban planners envisage a future in which most residents can reach essential services on foot.
ex.zh: 城市規劃者設想，未來大多數居民都能步行到達提供基本服務的場所。

col: as originally envisaged｜按最初的設想
words.tip: 後接名詞、動名詞或that從句，不接to do。

tr: vt. 想像, 預想
想像；展望
def: v. picture to oneself; imagine possible
to imagine a future situation or possibility

ex.en: I envision a small garden behind our new house.
ex.zh: 我想像著新家後面有一座小花園。

ex.en: Urban planners envision a future in which most residents can reach essential services on foot.
ex.zh: 城市規劃者展望這樣的未來：大多數居民步行即可享用基本服務。

col: envision a world｜設想一個世界
words.tip: 後接名詞或動名詞，不接to do。

疾病的一次發作
def: n. a happening that is distinctive in a series of related events

n. a part of a broadcast serial

ex.en: We watched the final episode together after dinner.
ex.zh: 晚飯後，我們一起看了最後一集。

ex.en: Each episode of the documentary explores how urban development affects wildlife in different parts of the world.
ex.zh: 這部紀錄片每一集都探討城市發展如何影響世界不同地區的野生動物。

col: a brief episode｜一段短暫經歷
words.tip: episode指一集；series指整部系列或連續劇。

tr: a. 插曲似的
def: s. of writing or narration; divided into or composed of episodes
s. occurring or appearing at usually irregular intervals
s. limited in duration to a single episode

tr: n. 渾名, 綽號, 稱號
def: n. descriptive word or phrase

def: n. a brief abstract (as of an article or book)

tr: vt. 摘要, 概括
def: v embody the essential characteristics of or be a typical example of

tr: n. 新紀元, 時代, 時期
時代；紀元
世（地質時間單位）
def: n. (astronomy) an arbitrarily fixed date that is the point in time relative to which information (as coordinates of a celestial body) is recorded
n. a unit of geological time that is a subdivision of a period and is itself divided into ages
a period of history marked by distinctive events or changes

ex.en: These old photographs capture an epoch of rapid change.
ex.zh: 這些老照片記錄了一個迅速變革的時代。

ex.en: The development of agriculture marked a new epoch in human history, transforming settlement patterns and social organisation.
ex.zh: 農業的發展標誌著人類歷史進入了一個新時代，改變了聚居模式和社會組織形式。

col: mark an epoch｜標誌一個時代的開啟
words.tip: 比 period 更強調時代特徵；地質學中譯為“世”。

tr: a. 平靜的, 變動小的
def: s. not varying
s. not easily irritated

n. the act of regarding as equal

tr: n. 赤道
[醫] 赤道, 中緯線
赤道
def: n. an imaginary line around the Earth forming the great circle that is equidistant from the north and south poles
n. a circle dividing a sphere or other surface into two usually equal and symmetrical parts
An imaginary line around Earth's middle, equally distant from both poles.

ex.en: Our guide explained why it stays warm near the equator.
ex.zh: 導遊解釋了為什麼赤道附近一直很暖和。

ex.en: Regions near the equator receive intense sunlight throughout the year, contributing to consistently high temperatures.
ex.zh: 赤道附近的地區全年受到強烈的陽光照射，因此氣溫持續偏高。

col: north of the equator｜赤道以北
words.tip: 赤道前通常加the；形容詞是equatorial。

tr: a. 騎術的, 馬的, 騎在馬背上的
n. 騎手
def: a. of or relating to or composed of knights
a. of or relating to or featuring horseback riding

[化] 平衡
平衡；均衡狀態
心情平靜；心理平衡
def: n. a stable situation in which forces cancel one another
n. a sensory system located in structures of the inner ear that registers the orientation of the head
A stable state in which opposing forces or influences balance.

ex.en: The hanging mobile regained equilibrium when I moved one ornament.
ex.zh: 我移動了一個飾物後，懸掛的裝飾架恢復了平衡。

ex.en: Removing a major predator can disturb the equilibrium of an ecosystem and cause unexpected changes in animal populations.
ex.zh: 移除主要捕食者可能破壞生態系統的平衡，並導致動物種群出現意想不到的變化。

words.tip: 通常不可數；常用於經濟、生態或物理中的平衡。

tr: n. 馬
a. 馬的, 象馬的
def: n. hoofed mammals having slender legs and a flat coat with a narrow mane along the back of the neck
a. resembling a horse
a. of or belonging to the family Equidae

tr: a. 公平的, 公正的
[法] 公平的, 公正的, 平衡法的
公平合理的；公正的
def: a. fair to all parties as dictated by reason and conscience
fair to everyone involved, taking their different circumstances into account

ex.en: We agreed on an equitable division of household chores.
ex.zh: 我們商定了公平合理的家務分工。

ex.en: An equitable funding system would direct more resources towards schools serving disadvantaged communities.
ex.zh: 公平合理的撥款制度會將更多資源投向服務弱勢社區的學校。

words.tip: equitable強調按情況公平，不一定是equal的均等。

tr: n. 公平, 公正
[經] 權益, 產權

n. the ownership interest of shareholders in a corporation

tr: n. 同等物, 等價物, 相等物

[計] 等價的
等值的；相當的
對應物；等值物
def: n. a person or thing equal to another in value or measure or force or effect or significance etc
n. the atomic weight of an element that has the same combining capacity as a given weight of another element; the standard is 8 for oxygen
s. being essentially equal to something

ex.en: This small heater produces heat equivalent to that larger one.
ex.zh: 這臺小取暖器產生的熱量與那臺較大的相當。

ex.en: Employers should recognise overseas qualifications when they are equivalent to those awarded by domestic institutions.
ex.zh: 當海外學歷與本國院校頒發的學歷相當時，僱主應予以認可。

col: the equivalent of｜相當於……的事物
words.tip: 常用equivalent to；相當不代表完全相同。

tr: a. 意義不明確的, 模稜兩可的

s. open to question
s. uncertain as a sign or indication

def: v be deliberately ambiguous or unclear in order to mislead or withhold information

tr: vt. 根除, 撲滅, 根絕, 消滅
根除；徹底消滅
def: v kill in large numbers
v destroy completely, as if down to the roots
To completely remove or destroy something harmful.

ex.en: We removed every root to eradicate weeds from the garden.
ex.zh: 我們清除了每一處草根，以徹底除去花園裡的雜草。

ex.en: International vaccination programmes aim to eradicate infectious diseases by ensuring that vulnerable populations receive adequate protection.
ex.zh: 國際疫苗接種計劃旨在確保易感人群得到充分保護，從而根除傳染病。

words.tip: 強調徹底消除，語氣強於reduce，常用於疾病或貧困。

tr: vt. 抹去, 擦掉
[計] 清洗; 擦除; 抹除; DOS內部命令:從磁盤上刪除一個或多個文件
def: v. remove from memory or existence
v. remove by or as if by rubbing or erasing
v. wipe out digitally or magnetically recorded information

tr: a. 直立的, 豎立的, 筆直的
vt. 使豎立, 使直立, 樹立, 建立
vi. 勃起
搭建；豎立
直立的；挺直的
def: a. upright in position or posture
to build something or put it in an upright position
standing straight up rather than bending or lying down

ex.en: We erected our tent beside the lake before sunset.
ex.zh: 日落前，我們在湖邊搭好了帳篷。

ex.en: Local authorities plan to erect temporary shelters for families whose homes were damaged by severe flooding.
ex.zh: 地方政府計劃搭建臨時住所，安置房屋因嚴重洪災受損的家庭。

words.tip: 動詞比 build 正式；形容詞常見於 stand erect。

tr: vt. 腐蝕, 侵蝕
vi. 受腐蝕
侵蝕；風化
逐漸削弱；損害
def: v. become ground down or deteriorate
v. remove soil or rock
To gradually wear away soil or rock through natural forces.

ex.en: Strong waves have eroded the cliffs near our village.
ex.zh: 強勁的海浪侵蝕了我們村莊附近的懸崖。

ex.en: Persistent inflation can erode household savings, making it harder for families to afford essential goods.
ex.zh: 持續的通貨膨脹會削弱家庭儲蓄的購買力，使家庭更難負擔生活必需品。

col: erode public trust｜削弱公眾信任
words.tip: 可指自然侵蝕，也可指信任、價值等逐漸受損。

tr: n. 任務, 差使, 使命
跑腿的差事
def: n. a short trip that is taken in the performance of a necessary task or mission
A short trip to buy, collect, or deliver something

ex.en: I ran an errand before meeting you for lunch.
ex.zh: 和你見面吃午飯前，我出去辦了點事。

ex.en: Reliable neighbourhood transport helps older residents run errands independently and maintain regular contact with their communities.
ex.zh: 可靠的社區交通能幫助老年居民獨立外出辦事，並與社區保持日常聯繫。

col: send someone on an errand｜派某人跑腿
a quick errand｜很快能辦完的差事
words.tip: 通常指外出辦小事；常搭配run errands。

火山噴發；噴出
突然爆發
def: v. start abruptly
v. erupt or intensify suddenly
v. start to burn or burst into flames

ex.en: We watched the volcano erupt in a nature documentary.
ex.zh: 我們在一部自然紀錄片裡看到了火山噴發。

ex.en: When volcanoes erupt, clouds of ash can disrupt air travel and affect communities far from the crater.
ex.zh: 火山噴發時，火山灰雲可能擾亂航空運輸，並影響遠離火山口的社區。

col: erupt into applause｜突然爆發掌聲
words.tip: 通常作不及物動詞；erupt into後可接掌聲等。

tr: vt. 避開, 遠避

護送；陪同
護送者；陪同人員
def: n. the act of accompanying someone or something in order to protect them
n. an attendant who is employed to accompany someone
v. accompany as an escort

ex.zh: 一名工作人員陪同我們去了候診室。

ex.en: Trained volunteers can escort elderly residents to medical appointments, improving access to essential healthcare services.
ex.zh: 受過培訓的志願者可以陪同老年居民就醫，從而改善他們獲得基本醫療服務的機會。

col: escort someone to｜陪同某人前往

words.tip: 動詞重音在後；名詞英/ˈeskɔːt/，美/ˈeskɔːrt/。

ex.zh: 這兩部手機除了顏色不同，基本上是一樣的。

ex.en: Although teaching methods have changed, the purpose of education remains essentially the same across generations.
ex.zh: 儘管教學方法有所改變，教育的目的在不同世代之間仍基本一致。

個人全部財產；遺產

n. extensive landed property (especially in the country) retained by the owner for his own use
A large area of owned land, often with a large house.

ex.en: We walked past the lake on the old country estate.
ex.zh: 我們步行經過那座古老鄉間莊園裡的湖泊。

ex.en: New housing estates should include green spaces and reliable transport links to nearby employment centres.
ex.zh: 新建住宅區應配備綠地，以及通往附近就業中心的可靠交通連接。

words.tip: real estate指房地產；housing estate指住宅區。

tr: a. 可尊敬的, 可估計的

s. deserving of esteem and respect

v. arouse hostility or indifference in where there had formerly been love, affection, or friendliness

v arouse hostility or indifference in where there had formerly been love, affection, or friendliness

無休止的；沒完沒了的
def: s continuing forever or indefinitely
s tiresomely long; seemingly without end
Lasting forever, without an end.

ex.en: The couple promised eternal love beneath the flowering tree.
ex.zh: 那對情侶在開花的樹下許下了永恆相愛的諾言。

ex.en: Many ancient cultures used monumental architecture to express hopes for eternal life and preserve collective memories.
ex.zh: 許多古代文化通過宏偉建築表達對永生的期盼，並保存集體記憶。

words.tip: eternal強調無終點；eternal complaints可誇張指抱怨不斷。

tr: a. 輕的, 飄渺的, 天上的
[醫] 醚制的, 揮發性的

s. characterized by unusual lightness and delicacy

def: n. (anthropology) the distinctive spirit of a culture or an era

tr: n. 語源, 語源學
def: n. a history of a word
n. the study of the sources and development of words

tr: a. 優生學的, 優種的

def: a. pertaining to or causing improvement in the offspring produced

tr: vt. 稱讚, 頌揚

tr: a. 委婉的
def: a. substituting a mild term for a harsher or distasteful one

tr: a. 音響好的, 悅耳的, 聲音和諧的
def: a. having a pleasant sound
s. (of speech or dialect) pleasing in sound; not harsh or strident

tr: n. 興奮, 陶醉, 陶醉感
[醫] 精神愉快, 欣快
def: n. a feeling of great (usually exaggerated) elation

tr: a. 欣快症的, 欣快的

def: a. exaggerated feeling of well-being or elation

v. empty completely
v. move people from their homes or country

def: v. practice evasion
v. use cunning or deceit to escape or avoid

tr: n. 評估, 估價, 求值
[計] 鑑定; 評價; 求值
評估；評價
def: n. act of ascertaining or fixing the value or worth of
n. an appraisal of the value of something
the process of judging something's quality, value, or effectiveness

ex.en: The coach's evaluation helped me improve my swimming technique.
ex.zh: 教練的評價幫助我改進了游泳技術。

ex.en: Regular evaluation of educational programmes allows schools to identify weaknesses and allocate resources more effectively.
ex.zh: 定期評估教育項目能幫助學校發現不足，並更有效地分配資源。

col: carry out an evaluation｜開展評估
words.tip: 常接of；強調質量或效果，價格估值常用valuation。

tr: a. 逐漸消失的, 容易消散的, 短暫的
[醫] 易消滅的, 漸消失的, 揮發性的
def: s. tending to vanish like vapor

tr: n. 逃避, 藉口
[法] 迴避, 規避, 逃避
def: n. a statement that is not literally false but that cleverly avoids an unpleasant truth
n. the deliberate act of failing to pay money
n. nonperformance of something distasteful (as by deceit or trickery) that you are supposed to do

tr: a. 逃避的, 迴避的, 託辭的
[法] 逃避的, 規避的, 推託的
def: s. deliberately vague or ambiguous
s. avoiding or escaping from difficulty or danger especially enemy fire

tr: a. 性情平和的
def: s not easily irritated

tr: a. 公平的, 公平無私的
def: s. without partiality

tr: a. 變故多的, 多事的, 重要的
多事的；經歷豐富的
def: a. full of events or incidents
Full of important, interesting, or unexpected events.

ex.en: After an eventful morning, we finally sat down for lunch.
ex.zh: 經歷了狀況不斷的一上午後，我們終於坐下來吃午飯。

ex.en: An eventful period of political reform transformed the country's education system and expanded access to schooling.
ex.zh: 一段大事頻發的政治改革時期改變了該國的教育體系，並擴大了入學機會。

col: an eventful day｜事情很多的一天
an eventful journey｜狀況不斷的旅程
an eventful life｜經歷豐富的一生
words.tip: 指發生許多值得注意的事，不一定都是壞事。

tr: a. 最後的, 終於的
def: s. expected to follow in the indefinite future from causes already operating

tr: n. 常綠樹, 常綠植物
a. 常綠的
def: n. a plant having foliage that persists and remains green throughout the year
a. (of plants and shrubs) bearing foliage throughout the year

tr: a. 永恆的, 持久的
n. 上帝, 神
永恆的；永久的
def: n. any of various plants of various genera of the family Compositae having flowers that can be dried without loss of form or color
Lasting forever or seeming never to end.

ex.en: They promised each other everlasting friendship beneath the old tree.
ex.zh: 他們在老樹下許下了友誼長存的承諾。

ex.en: Although digital storage appears to offer everlasting access, files can become unreadable as technology changes.
ex.zh: 雖然數字存儲似乎能讓資料永久可用，但技術變化可能導致文件無法讀取。

words.tip: 語氣比long-lasting更強，常用於愛、友誼等抽象事物。

tr: vt. 逐出, 趕出, 驅逐
[法] 逐出, 驅逐, 沒收
依法驅逐租戶等
def: v. expel or eject without recourse to legal process
v. expel from one's property or force to move out by a legal process
To legally force someone to leave a property

ex.en: The landlord threatened to evict us over unpaid rent.
ex.zh: 房東威脅要因我們拖欠房租而將我們趕走。

ex.en: Stronger tenant protections could prevent landlords from evicting vulnerable families without adequate notice or legal justification.
ex.zh: 加強租戶保護，可以防止房東在未充分提前通知或缺乏法律依據的情況下驅逐弱勢家庭。

col: evict someone from a property｜將某人逐出房產
words.tip: 常用evict somebody from；尤其指依法逐出租屋。

tr: n. 邪惡, 不幸, 罪惡
a. 邪惡的, 不幸的, 有害的, 討厭的
邪惡的；惡毒的
邪惡；罪惡；禍害
def: n. morally objectionable behavior
n. that which causes harm or destruction or misfortune; the good is oft interred with their bones"- Shakespeare
n. the quality of being morally wrong in principle or practice

ex.en: In the story, an evil wizard steals everyone's dreams.
ex.zh: 故事裡，一個邪惡的巫師偷走了所有人的夢。

ex.en: Literature often explores the conflict between good and evil through characters who face difficult moral choices.
ex.zh: 文學作品常通過面臨艱難道德選擇的人物，探討善與惡的衝突。

col: a necessary evil｜不得已接受的壞事
words.tip: 比bad語氣強得多，通常涉及嚴重的道德惡行。

tr: vt. 表明(感情等), 表示出(特性等)

tr: vt. 取出內臟, 除去精華, 切除(病人)器官
vi. (因手術不良)內臟凸出
def: v. remove the contents of
v. take away a vital or essential part of
s. having been disembowelled

tr: a. 喚出...的, 喚起...的
def: s. serving to bring to mind

tr: vt. 喚起, 引起, 召(魂)
[法] 提審, 移送
喚起；引起
def: v call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)
v evoke or provoke to appear or occur
v deduce (a principle) or construe (a meaning)

ex.en: The smell of fresh bread evokes memories of home.
ex.zh: 新鮮麵包的香味喚起了對家的回憶。

ex.en: Traditional music can evoke a strong sense of belonging among people living far from their homeland.
ex.zh: 傳統音樂能在遠離故土的人們心中喚起強烈的歸屬感。

words.tip: 直接接情感、回憶等賓語，不加of。

tr: vt. 使惡化, 使增劇, 激怒, 使加劇
def: v. exasperate or irritate

tr: n. 正確(性), 精密, 精確(性), 嚴格
def: n the quality of being exact

tr: v. 誇大, 誇張
def: v to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
v do something to an excessive degree

tr: n. 誇張, 誇大的事物, 誇大之詞
def: n. the act of making something more noticeable than usual
n. making to seem more important than it really is

tr: vt. 提升, 提高, 讚揚, 使得意
vi. 使人興奮, 使人得意
高度讚揚；頌揚
提升地位
def: v. raise in rank, character, or status
To praise someone or something very highly.
To raise someone to a higher rank or position.

ex.en: Her songs exalt the beauty of ordinary life.
ex.zh: 她的歌曲頌揚平凡生活中的美。

ex.en: Public monuments often exalt national heroes while overlooking the contributions of ordinary citizens.
ex.zh: 公共紀念碑往往頌揚民族英雄，卻忽視普通公民的貢獻。

col: exalt the virtues of｜盛讚……的美德
exalt someone to a position｜將某人提升至某職位
words.tip: 正式用詞；指高度頌揚，不是普通的表揚。

tr: n. 提升, 提高, 得意洋洋
[醫] [異常]興奮, 激越
def: n. the location of a planet in the zodiac at which it is believed to exert its maximum influence
n. a flock of larks (especially a flock of larks in flight overhead)

tr: a. 高尚的, 尊貴的, 高位的, 興奮的
def: s. of high moral or intellectual value; elevated in nature or style

tr: vt. 使惱怒, 激怒, 惡化
a. 糙面的, 惱怒的, 激怒的
使惱怒；使不耐煩
def: v exasperate or irritate
v make furious
v make worse

ex.en: The printer's constant paper jams exasperate everyone in our office.
ex.zh: 打印機不停卡紙，讓辦公室裡每個人都煩透了。

ex.en: Repeated delays in public transport can exasperate commuters and reduce their willingness to leave cars at home.
ex.zh: 公共交通反覆延誤會令通勤者惱火，降低他們放棄開車出行的意願。

words.tip: 勿混淆exacerbate：後者表示使問題惡化。

tr: n. 惱怒, 惱怒的原因
惱怒；忍無可忍
def: n. actions that cause great irritation (or even anger)
strong annoyance caused by repeated problems or irritating behaviour

ex.en: She sighed in exasperation when the printer jammed again.
ex.zh: 打印機又卡紙了，她惱火地嘆了口氣。

ex.en: Repeated delays in public transport can cause widespread exasperation and reduce confidence in local authorities.
ex.zh: 公共交通反覆延誤會引發普遍的不滿，並削弱公眾對地方政府的信任。

col: a sigh of exasperation｜惱火的嘆息
words.tip: 表示煩到失去耐心；勿與加劇混淆。

tr: v. 挖空, 挖出, 鑿通
挖掘；開鑿
發掘古蹟或遺物
def: v. recover through digging
v. find by digging in the ground
v. form by hollowing

ex.en: Workers excavated a deep hole for our new pool.
ex.zh: 工人們為我們的新游泳池挖了一個深坑。

ex.en: Archaeologists excavate ancient settlements to discover how earlier communities adapted to environmental changes and developed farming techniques.
ex.zh: 考古學家發掘古代聚落，以瞭解早期群體如何適應環境變化並發展耕作技術。

col: excavate ancient remains｜發掘古代遺存
words.tip: excavate可用於工程挖掘，也可用於考古發掘。

tr: a. 可反對的, 可抗議的

罕見的；特殊的
def: s. deviating widely from a norm of physical or mental ability; used especially of children below normal in intelligence
far better than usual
unusual and outside normal circumstances

ex.en: The young violinist gave an exceptional performance last night.
ex.zh: 那位年輕的小提琴手昨晚的演奏十分出色。

ex.en: Students with exceptional ability may require additional challenges to remain engaged in classroom learning.
ex.zh: 能力出眾的學生可能需要更有挑戰性的任務，才能持續投入課堂學習。

words.tip: 常指特別優秀；exceptional circumstances指特殊情況。

tr: n. 摘錄
v. 引用, 摘錄

a. 過量的, 額外的
過量；過剩
過量的；多餘的
def: n. a quantity much larger than is needed
n. immoderation as a consequence of going beyond sufficient or permitted limits
s. more than is needed, desired, or required

ex.en: Wipe away the excess paint with a clean cloth.
ex.zh: 用乾淨的布擦去多餘的油漆。

ex.en: Consuming sugar in excess can increase the risk of obesity and other health problems.
ex.zh: 攝入過量糖分會增加肥胖及其他健康問題的風險。

words.tip: in excess指過量；in excess of指超過某數量。

tr: a. 過度的, 過多的, 極端的
[法] 過度的, 過分的, 額外的
過量的；過度的
def: s. beyond normal limits
s. unrestrained, especially with regard to feelings
Greater than is necessary, reasonable, or acceptable.

ex.en: The excessive heat made our afternoon walk uncomfortable.
ex.zh: 酷熱讓我們下午的散步變得很不舒服。

ex.en: Excessive use of private cars contributes to urban air pollution and places pressure on existing roads.
ex.zh: 過度使用私家車加劇了城市空氣汙染，也給現有道路帶來壓力。

words.tip: 含超過合理限度之意，不等於extra（額外的）。

tr: adv. 過多, 極度, 過度, 過分
def: r. to a degree exceeding normal or proper limits

tr: n. (煙、酒等)消費稅, 貨物稅, 國產稅
vt. 切除
def: n. a tax that is measured by the amount of business done (not on property or income from real estate)
v. levy an excise tax on
v. remove by cutting

tr: n. 易興奮性, 興奮性, 激動性
[醫] 應激性, 刺激感受性, 興奮性
def: n. excessive sensitivity of an organ or body part
n. being easily excited

tr: vt. 刺激, 使興奮, 激勵
使興奮；使激動
激起；引發
def: v. arouse or elicit a feeling
v. raise to a higher energy level
v. produce a magnetic field in

ex.en: Trips to the seaside always excite my younger sister.
ex.zh: 去海邊玩總能讓我妹妹興奮不已。

ex.en: Interactive science exhibitions can excite young visitors and encourage them to explore scientific ideas independently.
ex.zh: 互動式科學展覽能讓年輕參觀者興奮起來，並鼓勵他們自主探索科學概念。

words.tip: 人感到興奮用excited；事物令人興奮用exciting。

tr: v. 大叫, 呼喊, 大聲叫
驚叫；大聲說
def: v. utter aloud; often with surprise, horror, or joy
to say something suddenly and loudly because of strong emotion

ex.en: “What a beautiful rainbow!” she exclaimed, pointing towards the hills.
ex.zh: “多美的彩虹啊！”她指著群山驚歎道。

ex.en: Visitors often exclaim in surprise when museum displays reveal the impressive engineering skills of ancient societies.
ex.zh: 當博物館展品展現古代社會令人讚歎的工程技藝時，參觀者往往驚歎不已。

words.tip: 強調因強烈情緒突然出聲，常用於引述話語。

tr: n. 驚呼, 激烈言詞, 驚歎詞
def: n. an abrupt excited utterance
n. a loud complaint or protest or reproach

tr: adv. 排他地, 僅僅, 專門, 只, 僅, 唯一地, 專有地
def: r without any others being included or involved

tr: vt. 想出, 研究出, 設計, 發明
def: v come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort
v reflect deeply on a subject

tr: vt. 剝皮, 擦破皮膚, 嚴厲的責難
def: v express strong disapproval of
v tear or wear off the skin or make sore by abrading

tr: vt. 排洩, 分泌
[醫] 排洩, 分泌
def: v. eliminate from the body

tr: vt. 施酷刑, 拷問, 使苦惱, 折磨
def: v torment emotionally or mentally
v subject to torture

tr: vt. 使無罪, 開脫
[法] 使無罪, 申辯無罪, 辯解
def: v pronounce not guilty of criminal charges

tr: a. 遊覽的, 離題的, 散漫的
[醫] 移動性的
def: s (of e.g. speech and writing) tending to depart from the main point or cover a wide range of subjects

tr: a. 該咒的, 可憎恨的, 討厭的
def: s of very poor quality or condition
s unequivocally detestable
s deserving a curse

tr: vt. 憎恨, 憎惡, 詛咒
vi. 詛咒
def: v find repugnant
v curse or declare to be evil or anathema or threaten with divine punishment

tr: vt. 執行, 實行, 完成, 處死, 製成
[計] 執行
def: v. kill as a means of socially sanctioned punishment
v. murder in a planned fashion
v. carry out the legalities of

tr: n. 模範, 榜樣, 原型, 標本

tr: a. 可仿效的, 可做模範的, 懲戒性的, 示範的
[法] 懲罰性的, 警戒性的, 示範的
def: s. worthy of imitation

tr: vt. 例證, 例示
[法] 製作經公章證明的謄本, 例證
是…的典型；例證
舉例說明
def: v. be characteristic of
v. clarify by giving an example of
to be a clear example of something

ex.en: Her handmade bowls exemplify the beauty of simple design.
ex.zh: 她手工製作的碗體現了簡約設計之美。

ex.en: These community gardens exemplify how urban residents can improve local biodiversity while producing fresh food.
ex.zh: 這些社區花園展示了城市居民如何在種植新鮮食物的同時改善當地生物多樣性。

col: exemplify a trend｜是某種趨勢的典型
exemplify a principle｜例證某項原則
exemplify the benefits of｜體現…的益處
words.tip: 及物動詞，直接接名詞；舉例時也可用be exemplified by。

tr: n. 免稅者, 被免除義務者
a. 免除的
vt. 使免除, 豁免
獲豁免的；被免除的
豁免；免除
def: v. grant relief or an exemption from a rule or requirement to
a. (of persons) freed from or not subject to an obligation or liability (as e.g. taxes) to which others or other things are subject
Not required to follow a rule or fulfil an obligation.

ex.en: Children under five are exempt from the entrance fee.
ex.zh: 五歲以下兒童免門票。

ex.en: Governments could exempt small businesses from certain taxes to encourage investment and support local employment.
ex.zh: 政府可以免除小企業的某些稅款，以鼓勵投資並支持當地就業。

words.tip: 固定搭配：be exempt from；exempt sb from。

tr: vt. 發揮, 運用, 施以影響
[法] 施加, 產生, 行使
施加；運用
使自己努力；盡力
def: v. put to use
v. make a great effort at a mental or physical task
To apply force, influence, or authority.

ex.en: You must exert steady pressure to open this lid.
ex.zh: 你得持續用力才能打開這個蓋子。

ex.en: Parents can exert considerable influence on children's eating habits by preparing balanced meals at home.
ex.zh: 父母可以通過在家準備營養均衡的飯菜，對孩子的飲食習慣產生很大影響。

words.tip: 常接pressure、influence；exert oneself意為盡力。

tr: v. 呼氣, 發出, 散發
def: v. expel air
v. give out (breath or an odor)

tr: n. 排氣, 排氣裝置, 廢氣
vt. 抽完, 用盡, 耗盡, 使精疲力盡
vi. 排氣
使精疲力竭
耗盡；用完

n. system consisting of the parts of an engine through which burned gases or steam are discharged
v. wear out completely

ex.en: Carrying those heavy boxes upstairs completely exhausted me.
ex.zh: 把那些沉重的箱子搬上樓讓我筋疲力盡。

ex.en: Intensive farming can exhaust soil nutrients, reducing agricultural productivity and increasing dependence on artificial fertilisers.
ex.zh: 集約化耕作可能耗盡土壤養分，降低農業生產力，並增加對化肥的依賴。

col: exhaust natural resources｜耗盡自然資源
exhaust all possibilities｜嘗試所有可能的辦法
words.tip: exhausted 指人累極了；exhausting 指事物令人疲憊。

tr: a. 消耗的, 枯竭的, 徹底的, 詳盡的
def: s. performed comprehensively and completely

tr: vt. 使高興, 使愉快, 鼓勵
使興奮；使振奮
def: v. fill with sublime emotion
To make someone feel excited, energetic, and very happy

ex.en: The fast boat ride exhilarated everyone on board.
ex.zh: 快艇飛馳讓船上的每個人都興奮不已。

ex.en: Outdoor adventures can exhilarate participants while helping them develop confidence and a stronger connection with nature.
ex.zh: 戶外探險能讓參與者精神振奮，同時幫助他們增強自信，加深與自然的聯繫。

col: exhilarated by the experience｜因這次經歷而振奮
an exhilarating experience｜令人興奮的經歷
words.tip: 及物動詞；人感到興奮用exhilarated。

tr: n. 令人高興, 愉快
def: n. the feeling of lively and cheerful joy

tr: vt. 掘出, 發掘
def: v dig up for reburial or for medical investigation; of dead bodies

tr: n. 緊急, 急迫, 緊急事件
def: n. a pressing or urgent situation

tr: a. 緊急的, 迫切的, 苛求的
[法] 催告書, 勒令, 限令
def: s. requiring precise accuracy

def: s. extremely scanty

tr: n. 大批的離去
[法] 退出, 大批離去, 成一外出
def: n. a journey by a large group to escape from a hostile environment

n. the second book of the Old Testament: tells of the departure of the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt led by Moses; God gave them the Ten Commandments and the rest of Mosaic law on Mount Sinai during the Exodus

tr: vt. 免除, 證明無罪
[法] 解放, 開釋, 免罪
def: v pronounce not guilty of criminal charges

tr: n. 免罪, 免除
[經] 免除, 解除, 免於
洗清罪名；免責
def: n. the condition of being relieved from blame or obligation
An official finding that someone is not guilty or responsible.

ex.en: Her exoneration brought relief to the whole family.
ex.zh: 她獲證清白，讓全家都鬆了一口氣。

ex.en: The exoneration of wrongly convicted individuals demonstrates why legal systems must allow new evidence to be reviewed.
ex.zh: 被錯誤定罪者獲證清白，說明司法體系必須允許重新審查新證據。

col: lead to exoneration｜使人獲證清白
words.tip: 強調證明無罪或無責；pardon指赦免。

tr: a. 過度的, 過高的, 過分的
價格過高的；收費離譜的
def: s. greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
Much higher in price or cost than is reasonable.

ex.en: The hotel charged an exorbitant amount for breakfast.
ex.zh: 這家酒店的早餐收費高得離譜。

ex.en: Exorbitant rents in major cities can force essential workers to live far from their places of employment.
ex.zh: 大城市過高的租金可能迫使關鍵崗位的勞動者住在遠離工作地點的地方。

words.tip: 比expensive語氣更強，含不合理、過高之意。

tr: vt. 驅邪, 除怪
def: v. expel through adjuration or prayers

tr: a. 異國的, 外來的
n. 外來人, 外來物, 舶來品
異國情調的；奇異的
外來的；非本土的
def: s. strikingly strange or unusual
Unusual and interesting, especially because of a connection with distant countries.
Originating outside the region where something is now found.

ex.en: The market sells exotic fruits I have never tasted.
ex.zh: 市場裡賣著我從未嘗過的異國水果。

ex.en: Introducing exotic plants into local gardens can threaten native species if their spread is not controlled.
ex.zh: 將外來植物引入當地花園後，若不控制其蔓延，可能會威脅本土物種。

col: exotic destination｜富有異國情調的目的地
words.tip: 生態語境中指非本土的，不一定具有入侵性。

tr: vt. 使膨脹, 詳述, 擴張
vi. 張開, 發展
vt. 展開
vi. 展開
[計] 展開; DOS外部命令:將原始DOS磁盤上的壓縮文件解壓縮並拷貝到硬盤上
def: v. extend in one or more directions
v. become larger in size or volume or quantity
v. make bigger or wider in size, volume, or quantity

ex.en: The dough expanded as it rested in the warm kitchen.
ex.zh: 麵糰在溫暖的廚房裡靜置時膨脹起來了。

ex.en: Universities should expand access to online courses while ensuring that disadvantaged students have adequate equipment and internet connections.
ex.zh: 大學應擴大在線課程的覆蓋範圍，同時確保弱勢學生擁有足夠的設備和網絡條件。

col: expand access to｜擴大獲得……的機會
expand on an idea｜進一步闡述想法
words.tip: “詳述”用expand on/upon；擴大某物可直接接賓語。

tr: vi. 詳述, 細說, 漫遊
def: v add details, as to an account or idea; clarify the meaning of and discourse in a learned way, usually in writing

tr: n. 移居國外者, 僑民, 被流放者, 背井離鄉者
vt. 逐出國外, 脫離國籍, 放逐
vi. 移居國外
def: v. expel from a country
v. move away from one's native country and adopt a new residence abroad

tr: n. 權宜, 方便, 私利
def: n the quality of being suited to the end in view

tr: n. 權宜之計
a. 權宜的, 方便的, 有用的
def: n. a means to an end; not necessarily a principled or ethical one
a. serving to promote your interest
s. appropriate to a purpose; practical

tr: a. 迅速的, 敏捷的
def: s. marked by speed and efficiency

tr: adv. 迅速(完成), 高效, 效率高, 敏捷, 急速(進行)
def: r with efficiency; in an efficient manner

tr: vt. 驅逐, 逐出, 排出, 開除
[醫] 排除, 迫出
def: v. force to leave or move out

tr: vt. 花費, 消耗, 用光
def: v use up, consume fully
v pay out

tr: n. 開支, 費用, 用光, 消費額
[經] 支出, 費用, 消費
支出；花費
精力或時間的消耗
def: n money paid out; an amount spent
n the act of spending money for goods or services
n the act of consuming something

ex.en: We track our monthly expenditure in a small notebook.
ex.zh: 我們用一個小本子記錄每月開支。

ex.en: Higher public expenditure on preventive healthcare could reduce the long-term cost of treating chronic diseases.
ex.zh: 增加預防性醫療的公共支出，可以降低治療慢性病的長期成本。

words.tip: 通常不可數；expenditure on後接花費對象。

tr: n. 專家意見, 專門技術
[法] 專門知識, 專家意見
專業知識；專門技能
def: n skillfulness by virtue of possessing special knowledge
Specialist knowledge or skills gained through training and experience.

ex.en: We need your expertise to repair this old clock.
ex.zh: 修理這座舊鐘需要你的專業技能。

ex.en: Universities can support local businesses by sharing their expertise in renewable energy and sustainable manufacturing.
ex.zh: 大學可以通過分享可再生能源和可持續製造領域的專業知識來支持當地企業。

col: draw on expertise｜利用專業知識
words.tip: 不可數；某領域的專長用expertise in。

tr: vt. 補償, 贖
vi. 抵償, 贖罪
def: v. make amends for

vt. 呼出
到期；失效
def: v lose validity
v pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
v expel air

ex.en: My passport expires next month, so I must renew it.
ex.zh: 我的護照下個月到期，所以必須換髮。

ex.en: When temporary work permits expire, employees may face uncertainty about their future employment and residence.
ex.zh: 臨時工作許可到期時，僱員的未來就業和居留可能面臨不確定性。

words.tip: 是不及物動詞：合同到期用expires，不用is expired。

tr: a. 說明的, 解釋的, 辯明的
[法] 解釋的, 說明的
解釋性的；說明的
def: s. serving or intended to explain or make clear
Giving information that makes something easier to understand.

ex.en: The recipe includes explanatory pictures for each tricky step.
ex.zh: 這份食譜為每個難操作的步驟都配上了說明圖片。

ex.en: Public health campaigns should provide explanatory materials that help people understand both the benefits and limitations of medical screening.
ex.zh: 公共衛生宣傳應提供說明材料，幫助人們瞭解醫學篩查的益處和侷限。

words.tip: 常修飾notes、material；self-explanatory指不言自明的。

明確的；直言的

expressed clearly and directly, leaving no doubt about the meaning

ex.en: Please give me explicit instructions for assembling this wooden shelf.
ex.zh: 請給我明確的說明，告訴我如何組裝這個木架。

ex.en: Schools should establish explicit rules about online behaviour to help students use digital platforms responsibly.
ex.zh: 學校應制定明確的網絡行為規範，幫助學生負責任地使用數字平臺。

words.tip: explicit指明說的；implicit指未明說但可推知的。

探索；探訪
探討；研究
def: v. travel to or penetrate into
v. examine minutely
v. examine (organs) for diagnostic purposes

ex.en: We spent the afternoon exploring narrow streets near the harbour.
ex.zh: 我們花了一下午探訪港口附近的狹窄街巷。

ex.en: Schools should encourage students to explore different career options before choosing subjects for further study.
ex.zh: 學校應鼓勵學生在選擇深造科目前探索不同的職業方向。

words.tip: 作及物動詞時直接接地點或問題，不加about。

def: v. reason with (somebody) for the purpose of dissuasion

def: n. vulnerability to the elements; to the action of heat or cold or wind or rain;
n. the act of subjecting someone to an influencing experience
n. the disclosure of something secret

tr: v. 詳細說明, 解釋
def: v add details, as to an account or idea; clarify the meaning of and discourse in a learned way, usually in writing
v state

tr: adv. 明白地, 清楚地, 特意地
明確地
專門地；特意地
def: r. with specific intentions; for the express purpose
in a clear and direct way that leaves no doubt
for a particular purpose

ex.en: I expressly asked for a room away from the lift.
ex.zh: 我明確要求安排一個遠離電梯的房間。

ex.en: Public funds allocated expressly for environmental protection should not be diverted to projects that increase industrial pollution.
ex.zh: 專門用於環境保護的公共資金，不應被挪用於加劇工業汙染的項目。

words.tip: 勿與expressively混淆，後者指富有表現力地。

tr: vt. 剝奪, 沒收, 徵用
[法] 徵用, 沒收, 剝奪...的所有權
def: v. deprive of possessions

tr: n. 逐出, 開除, 驅逐, 排氣
[醫] 逼出
開除；驅逐
排出；噴出
def: n. the act of expelling or projecting or ejecting
The act of officially forcing someone to leave a place.
The process of forcing something out of a space or body.

ex.en: Repeated cheating led to his expulsion from the club.
ex.zh: 反覆作弊導致他被俱樂部開除。

ex.en: Schools should consider supportive interventions before expulsion, as exclusion can seriously damage a young person's educational prospects.
ex.zh: 學校在開除學生之前應考慮採取支持性干預措施，因為排斥可能嚴重損害年輕人的教育前景。

words.tip: 常用expulsion from；對應動詞為expel。

tr: vt. 擦掉, 刪掉, 除去
def: v remove by erasing or crossing out or as if by drawing a line

tr: vt. 刪除, 修訂, 使純潔
def: v edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate

tr: a. 精緻的, 細膩的, 敏銳的
精美的；精緻的
極強烈的；極敏銳的
def: s. intense or sharp
s. lavishly elegant and refined
s. of extreme beauty

ex.en: She keeps an exquisite porcelain bowl on the shelf.
ex.zh: 她把一隻精美的瓷碗放在架子上。

ex.en: Museums preserve exquisite examples of traditional craftsmanship, allowing future generations to appreciate their cultural and artistic value.
ex.zh: 博物館保存傳統工藝的精美作品，讓後代能夠欣賞其文化與藝術價值。

words.tip: 常形容精美工藝；修飾pain時表示極其強烈。

tr: a. 現存的, 未毀的
def: a. still in existence; not extinct or destroyed or lost

tr: v. 即席演說, 即興演奏, 當場作成
def: v manage in a makeshift way; do with whatever is at hand
v perform without preparation

tr: v. 擴充, 延伸, 伸展, 擴大
[計] 擴展
延長；擴大
伸出；伸展
給予；表示
def: v. make available; provide
v. reach outward in space
v. expand the influence of

ex.en: We extended our holiday because the weather was so lovely.
ex.zh: 天氣實在太好了，我們便延長了假期。

ex.en: Governments should extend public transport networks to ensure that residents of outer suburbs can access employment opportunities.
ex.zh: 政府應擴大公共交通網絡，確保遠郊居民能夠獲得就業機會。

col: extend a deadline｜延長截止期限
extend a warm welcome｜表示熱烈歡迎
words.tip: extend by接增加量；extend to接新的終點或期限。

tr: n. 延長, 擴充, 範圍, 擴展名
a. 伸縮的
[計] 擴展名, 擴充名
def: n. a mutually agreed delay in the date set for the completion of a job or payment of a debt
n. act of expanding in scope; making more widely available
n. an educational opportunity provided by colleges and universities to people who are not enrolled as regular students

tr: a. 廣的, 廣泛的, 多方面的
[經] 廣大的, 擴大的
廣泛的；大量的
遼闊的；大面積的
def: s. large in spatial extent or range or scope or quantity
a. of agriculture; increasing productivity by using large areas with minimal outlay and labor
covering many subjects or involving a large amount

ex.en: The storm caused extensive damage to our roof.
ex.zh: 暴風雨使我們家的屋頂大面積受損。

ex.en: Extensive research is needed before governments introduce major changes to the national education system.
ex.zh: 政府對國家教育制度進行重大改革之前，需要開展廣泛研究。

words.tip: 強調範圍廣或數量多；intensive強調集中、強度高。

tr: vt. 減輕, 為...找藉口
[法] 減輕, 低估, 藐視
def: v. lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of

def: v. kill en masse; kill on a large scale; kill many

tr: vt. 給...以外型, 使客觀化, 使具體化
[醫] 表面化
def: v regard as objective
v make external or objective, or give reality to

tr: a. 熄滅的, 滅絕的, 耗盡的
[法] 消滅了的, 過時的, 無效的
滅絕的
死的；不再噴發的
def: a. no longer in existence; lost or especially having died out leaving no living representatives
a. (of e.g. volcanos) permanently inactive
s. being out or having grown cold

ex.en: My little cousin asked why dinosaurs became extinct.
ex.zh: 我的小表弟問恐龍為什麼滅絕了。

ex.en: Without stronger habitat protection, many endangered species could become extinct within the next few decades.
ex.zh: 如果不加強棲息地保護，許多瀕危物種可能在未來幾十年內滅絕。

words.tip: extinct指已滅絕；endangered指瀕危，尚未滅絕。

tr: n. 消失, 消滅, 廢止
[化] 消光; 熄滅
滅絕；消亡
def: n. no longer active; extinguished
n. no longer in existence
n. the reduction of the intensity of radiation as a consequence of absorption and radiation

ex.en: These rare birds face extinction if their forest disappears.
ex.zh: 如果這片森林消失，這些珍稀鳥類就會面臨滅絕。

ex.en: Protecting natural habitats is essential to preventing the extinction of species threatened by intensive farming and urban expansion.
ex.zh: 保護自然棲息地對於防止受集約化農業和城市擴張威脅的物種滅絕至關重要。

col: on the brink of extinction｜瀕臨滅絕
words.tip: extinct是形容詞；extinction是通常不可數的名詞。

tr: vt. 熄滅, 使消亡, 壓制, 使減色
[醫] 消滅
熄滅；撲滅
使希望等破滅；消除
def: v. terminate, end, or take out
to stop a fire or flame from burning
to bring a feeling, hope, or idea to an end

ex.en: We extinguished the campfire before getting into our tents.
ex.zh: 我們在進入帳篷前撲滅了篝火。

ex.en: Prolonged unemployment can extinguish young people's hopes of achieving financial independence and securing stable housing.
ex.zh: 長期失業可能使年輕人實現經濟獨立和獲得穩定住房的希望破滅。

words.tip: 及物動詞；日常說撲滅也可用put out。

tr: n. 消滅, 根除, 毀滅
[醫] 摘除
def: n. the act of pulling up or out; uprooting; cutting off from existence

tr: vt. 頌揚, 稱讚, 吹捧

v. obtain by coercion or intimidation
v. get or cause to become in a difficult or laborious manner

v. get despite difficulties or obstacles
v. separate (a metal) from an ore

ex.zh: 今天早上，牙醫小心地拔掉了那顆壞牙。

ex.zh: 研究人員從大型數據集中提取有用信息，以識別家庭能源消耗的規律。

col: an extract from a novel｜小說節選
words.tip: 動詞重音在後；名詞讀/ˈekstrækt/。

奢侈；揮霍

ex.zh: 每週買鮮花是我唯一的奢侈享受。

ex.en: Public criticism of government extravagance often increases when essential services face severe budget cuts.
ex.zh: 當基本公共服務面臨大幅預算削減時，公眾對政府鋪張浪費的批評往往會增加。

col: an unnecessary extravagance｜不必要的奢侈之舉
a taste for extravagance｜對奢華的偏愛
words.tip: 指揮霍行為通常不可數；指某項奢侈享受時可數。

growing abundantly or richly decorated and imaginative

ex.en: The exuberant puppy bounced around the garden all morning.
ex.zh: 那隻活力十足的小狗整個上午都在花園裡蹦來蹦去。

ex.en: Exuberant celebrations at international sporting events can create a powerful sense of shared identity among spectators.
ex.zh: 國際體育賽事中熱情洋溢的慶祝活動能讓觀眾產生強烈的共同認同感。

col: an exuberant personality｜熱情奔放的性格
words.tip: 核心是活力或豐富程度高，不等於“華而不實”。

tr: n. 織物, 布, 結構, 構造, 建築物

布料；織物
基本結構
def: n. artifact made by weaving or felting or knitting or crocheting natural or synthetic fibers
material made by weaving or knitting fibres
the connected parts that form a society or organisation

ex.en: This soft fabric will make a comfortable summer dress.
ex.zh: 這種柔軟的布料做夏季連衣裙會很舒服。

ex.en: Community centres strengthen the social fabric by bringing together residents from different cultural and economic backgrounds.
ex.zh: 社區中心讓不同文化與經濟背景的居民聚在一起，從而鞏固社會紐帶。

words.tip: 泛指布料常不可數；不同種類可用fabrics。

tr: vt. 製造, 建造, 裝配, 偽造
捏造；偽造
製造；裝配

To invent false information in order to deceive
To make a product or structure from separate materials

ex.en: He fabricated an excuse for missing the family dinner.
ex.zh: 他編了個藉口，解釋自己為什麼沒來參加家庭聚餐。

ex.en: Researchers who fabricate evidence undermine public trust in science and may influence important policy decisions.
ex.zh: 捏造證據的研究人員會損害公眾對科學的信任，並可能影響重要的政策決策。

words.tip: 既可指捏造信息，也可指工業製造，須看賓語。

tr: a. 傳說的, 寓言般的, 難以置信的
極好的；絕妙的
巨大的；驚人的
傳說中的
def: s. extremely pleasing
s. based on or told of in traditional stories; lacking factual basis or historical validity
s. barely credible

ex.en: We had a fabulous picnic beside the lake yesterday.
ex.zh: 昨天我們在湖邊度過了一段美妙的野餐時光。

ex.en: Although tourism can generate fabulous wealth, its economic benefits are not always shared fairly among local residents.
ex.zh: 儘管旅遊業能創造鉅額財富，其經濟收益卻並非總能在當地居民之間公平分配。

col: a fabulous time｜極其愉快的時光
words.tip: 表“極好的”多用於非正式語境，語氣較強。

tr: a. 滑稽的, 愛開玩笑的

tr: vt. 使容易, 促進, 幫助
[法] 使容易, 使便利, 推進
促進；使便利
def: v. make easier
v. increase the likelihood of (a response)
make an action or process easier

ex.en: These sliding doors facilitate access for people using wheelchairs.
ex.zh: 這些推拉門方便使用輪椅的人進出。

ex.en: Digital platforms can facilitate collaboration between students in different countries, allowing them to exchange ideas more easily.
ex.zh: 數字平臺可以促進不同國家學生之間的合作，讓他們更容易交流想法。

words.tip: 後接名詞或動名詞，不用facilitate somebody to do。

tr: a. 人為的, 人工的, 不自然的
[醫] 人工的, 人造的, 假的
def: s. not produced by natural forces

基於事實的；事實性的
def: a. of or relating to or characterized by facts
Based on facts rather than opinions or invented details.

ex.en: Her account of the accident was brief and factual.
ex.zh: 她對事故的敘述簡短且符合事實。

ex.en: Students should learn to distinguish factual information from personal opinion when evaluating sources for academic assignments.
ex.zh: 學生在評估學術作業所用的資料來源時，應學會區分事實信息與個人觀點。

words.tip: 強調依據事實，不等於actual所指的實際存在。

tr: n. 才能, 能力, 全體教員, (大學的)系
[醫] 能力, [大學]院系
大學的院；系
全體教員
官能；能力
def: n. one of the inherent cognitive or perceptual powers of the mind
A university division covering a particular group of subjects.
The teaching staff of a university, college, or school.

ex.en: The science faculty has moved into a new building.
ex.zh: 理學院已搬進一棟新樓。

ex.en: Cooperation between the faculty of engineering and local industries can help students develop skills relevant to employment.
ex.zh: 工程學院與當地產業的合作可以幫助學生培養與就業相關的技能。

words.tip: 英式常指大學院系，美式常指全體教員。

tr: n. 時尚
[化] 黃素腺嘌呤二核苷酸
def: n. an interest followed with exaggerated zeal

tr: a. 趨於時尚的, 風行的, 流行的
def: s. intensely fashionable for a short time

tr: vi. 褪色, 消失, 凋謝

褪色；使褪色
def: n. gradually ceasing to be visible
v. become less clearly visible or distinguishable; disappear gradually or seemingly
v. lose freshness, vigor, or vitality

ex.en: The curtains have faded after years of bright sunlight.
ex.zh: 窗簾經過多年強烈日曬，已經褪色了。

ex.en: Public interest in environmental campaigns may fade unless organisations provide regular updates and opportunities for participation.
ex.zh: 如果組織不定期提供最新進展和參與機會，公眾對環保活動的興趣可能會逐漸減退。

col: fade in the sun｜在陽光下褪色
fade into the background｜逐漸不再引人注意
words.tip: 強調逐漸變化；fade away指慢慢減弱或消失。

s. based on an incorrect or misleading notion or information

[醫] 錯覺, 幻覺, 虛妄
謬見；錯誤觀念
邏輯謬誤

A belief that is commonly accepted but actually false.
An error in reasoning that makes an argument unreliable.

ex.en: It is a fallacy that expensive shoes always last longer.
ex.zh: 認為昂貴的鞋子總是更耐穿，是一種錯誤觀念。

ex.en: The claim that economic growth automatically benefits every citizen rests on a fallacy about how wealth is distributed.
ex.zh: 經濟增長會自動惠及每位公民的說法，建立在對財富分配方式的錯誤認識之上。

words.tip: 不只是事實錯誤，也常指論證中的邏輯錯誤。

def: n. the likelihood of making errors

tr: a. 易錯的, 可能犯錯的
會犯錯的；不完全可靠的

s. wanting in moral strength, courage, or will; having the attributes of man as opposed to e.g. divine beings
Capable of making mistakes or being wrong

ex.en: Even experienced drivers are fallible, so please stay alert.
ex.zh: 即使經驗豐富的司機也會犯錯，所以請保持警覺。

ex.en: Human memory is fallible, which raises concerns about relying solely on eyewitness accounts in court.
ex.zh: 人的記憶可能出錯，因此在法庭上僅依賴目擊者陳述令人擔憂。

col: fallible human judgement｜可能出錯的人類判斷
a fallible system｜不完全可靠的系統
words.tip: 強調可能犯錯，並非一定錯誤；反義詞為infallible。

a severe shortage of food affecting many people

ex.zh: 我們社區向遭受饑荒的家庭運送了食物。

ex.en: Prolonged drought can lead to famine when farming communities lack reliable irrigation systems and emergency food reserves.
ex.zh: 當農業社區缺乏可靠的灌溉系統和應急糧食儲備時，長期乾旱可能導致饑荒。

words.tip: famine指大範圍糧食匱乏；個人飢餓用hunger。

tr: vt. 使捱餓

v deprive of food

Someone who is extremely enthusiastic about an activity or interest.

ex.en: My cousin is a fitness fanatic who exercises daily.
ex.zh: 我表親是個健身迷，每天都鍛鍊。

ex.en: A political fanatic may reject reasonable debate, making it harder for communities to resolve disagreements peacefully.
ex.zh: 政治狂熱者可能拒絕理性辯論，使社會群體更難和平解決分歧。

幻想；想像

n. fiction with a large amount of imagination in it
v. indulge in fantasies

ex.zh: 住在城堡裡是我童年時最喜歡的幻想。

ex.en: Fantasy literature can encourage young readers to explore moral questions through imaginary worlds and unusual characters.
ex.zh: 奇幻文學可以鼓勵年輕讀者通過虛構世界和不同尋常的角色探索道德問題。

words.tip: 具體幻想可數；表示奇幻文學類型時通常不可數。

n. the act of departing politely

ex.en: We gathered at the station for a final farewell.
ex.zh: 我們聚在車站，作最後的告別。

ex.en: A farewell ceremony can help graduating students reflect on their achievements and prepare for future challenges.
ex.zh: 告別儀式可以幫助畢業生回顧自己的成就，併為未來的挑戰做好準備。

words.tip: 比goodbye正式，常用於長久分別或鄭重告別。

tr: vt. 令人入神, 使著迷
vi. 入迷
使著迷；深深吸引
def: v. to render motionless, as with a fixed stare or by arousing terror or awe
to attract and hold someone's attention very strongly

ex.en: The colourful fish fascinated the children at the aquarium.
ex.zh: 水族館裡色彩斑斕的魚讓孩子們看得入迷。

ex.en: Ancient civilisations continue to fascinate researchers because their achievements reveal remarkable solutions to complex practical problems.
ex.zh: 古代文明仍然令研究者著迷，因為其成就展現瞭解決複雜實際問題的非凡方法。

col: fascinate an audience｜深深吸引觀眾
never cease to fascinate｜始終令人著迷
words.tip: 事物令人著迷用fascinating；人感到著迷用fascinated。

tr: a. 迷人的, 吸引人的, 使人神魂顛倒的
極有吸引力的；迷人的
def: v cause to be interested or curious
v to render motionless, as with a fixed stare or by arousing terror or awe
v attract; cause to be enamored

ex.en: The guide told us fascinating stories about the castle.
ex.zh: 導遊給我們講了關於這座城堡的精彩故事。

ex.en: Museum collections offer fascinating insights into how earlier societies adapted to changes in their natural environments.
ex.zh: 博物館藏品讓人們深入瞭解早期社會如何適應自然環境的變化，令人著迷。

words.tip: 事物令人著迷用fascinating；人著迷用fascinated。

tr: a. 快速的, 緊的

n. 絕食, 齋戒
vi. 絕食, 齋戒
快速的
def: n. abstaining from food
v. abstain from certain foods, as for religious or medical reasons
v. abstain from eating

ex.en: We caught a fast train and arrived before lunch.
ex.zh: 我們趕上了一班快車，在午飯前就到了。

ex.en: Fast internet connections allow rural businesses to reach wider markets and compete with companies in major cities.
ex.zh: 高速網絡連接使鄉村企業能夠進入更廣闊的市場，並與大城市的公司競爭。

words.tip: fast本身可作副詞，不能說fastly。

tr: vt. 拴緊, 使固定, 系, 集中於, 強加於
vi. 扣緊
扣緊；繫牢；固定
def: v. cause to be firmly attached
v. become fixed or fastened
v. attach to

ex.en: Please fasten your seat belt before we leave.
ex.zh: 出發前請繫好安全帶。

ex.en: Passengers must fasten their seat belts during takeoff and landing to reduce the risk of injury.
ex.zh: 乘客在飛機起飛和降落時必須繫好安全帶，以降低受傷風險。

col: fasten a seat belt｜繫好安全帶
words.tip: t不發音；反義詞unfasten表示解開。

tr: a. 難取悅的, 挑剔的, 苛求的
一絲不苟的；挑剔的

a. having complicated nutritional requirements; especially growing only in special artificial cultures
Very attentive to detail and difficult to satisfy.

ex.en: My brother is fastidious about keeping his shoes spotless.
ex.zh: 我哥哥對鞋子的清潔要求很高，總要保持一塵不染。

ex.en: Fastidious attention to hygiene in food preparation can reduce contamination risks and help maintain public confidence in restaurants.
ex.zh: 在備餐時一絲不苟地注意衛生，可以降低汙染風險，並幫助維持公眾對餐館的信任。

col: fastidious about cleanliness｜對清潔要求極嚴
fastidious attention to detail｜對細節的一絲不苟
words.tip: 可褒可貶：既指嚴謹細緻，也指過分挑剔。

tr: a. 致命的, 重大的, 命運註定的, 粗心的, 不幸的
[醫] 致命的, 致死的
致命的
毀滅性的；導致失敗的
def: a. bringing death
s. controlled or decreed by fate; predetermined
Causing someone's death.

ex.en: These wild mushrooms can be fatal if you eat them.
ex.zh: 這些野生蘑菇吃了可能會致命。

ex.en: Lower speed limits near schools can reduce the risk of fatal accidents involving pedestrians and cyclists.
ex.zh: 降低學校附近的限速可以減少涉及行人和騎車人的致命事故風險。

words.tip: fatal強調致死或導致失敗；fateful指影響重大的。

tr: n. 英尋(長度單位,合6英尺)

v. measure the depth of (a body of water) with a sounding line

tr: a. 預言的, 有預言能力的

a. 疲勞的
疲勞；疲乏

n. used of materials (especially metals) in a weakened state caused by long stress
n. (always used with a modifier) boredom resulting from overexposure to something

ex.en: After the long hike, fatigue made my legs shake.
ex.zh: 長途徒步後，我累得雙腿發抖。

ex.en: Persistent fatigue can reduce employees' concentration and increase the likelihood of accidents in the workplace.
ex.zh: 持續疲勞會降低員工的注意力，並增加工作場所發生事故的可能性。

words.tip: 通常為不可數名詞，比tiredness更正式。

tr: vi. 養肥
vt. 使肥胖
def: v. make fat or plump

tr: n. 愚鈍, 昏庸, 愚蠢言行
[醫] 愚昧
def: n a ludicrous folly

vt. 挑剔
vi. 產生斷層, 弄錯
[計] 故障
缺陷；故障
def: n. (geology) a crack in the earth's crust resulting from the displacement of one side with respect to the other
n. (electronics) equipment failure attributable to some defect in a circuit (loose connection or insulation failure or short circuit etc.)
n. responsibility for a bad situation or event

ex.en: A small electrical fault stopped the washing machine yesterday.
ex.zh: 昨天一個小小的電路故障讓洗衣機停止了運轉。

ex.en: Regular inspections can identify a structural fault before it threatens the safety of residents.

ex.zh: 我們聽從了導遊的警告，離開了海灘。

ex.en: Governments must heed scientific advice when developing policies to protect communities from extreme weather.
ex.zh: 政府制定保護社區免受極端天氣影響的政策時，必須重視科學建議。

ex.zh: 最初綻放的花朵預示著春天的到來。

ex.zh: 經濟實惠的儲能技術取得進步，可能預示著偏遠社區迎來可靠使用可再生電力的新時代。

ex.zh: 這些食草蜥蜴喜歡吃我們花園裡的新鮮葉子。

ex.zh: 食草動物通過吃掉幼苗和利用糞便傳播種子來影響森林生長。

words.tip: 不僅指吃草，也包括以樹葉、果實等植物為食。

ex.zh: 醫生詢問這種病是否可能具有遺傳性。

ex.zh: 遺傳諮詢可以幫助家庭瞭解遺傳性疾病，並對醫療保健作出知情決定。

words.tip: 可指基因遺傳，也可指頭銜世襲；遺傳不等於傳染。

ex.zh: 踏上那座窄橋前，她顯得有些猶豫。

ex.zh: 我們週末的徒步旅行在一片清澈的山間湖泊旁結束。

ex.zh: 公共交通票價大幅上漲可能會降低通勤者選擇公交車而非私家車的意願。

extremely funny and likely to make people laugh

ex.zh: 她那個特別好笑的故事讓大家吃飯時笑個不停。

ex.en: Although hilarious advertisements can attract attention, humour does not always help consumers remember the product being promoted.
ex.zh: 雖然令人捧腹的廣告能夠吸引注意，但幽默並不總能幫助消費者記住所推銷的產品。

words.tip: 強調“極其好笑”，不只是熱鬧或開心。

ex.en: Heavy snow hindered our journey through the mountains.
ex.zh: 大雪阻礙了我們穿越山區的行程。

ex.en: Limited access to reliable internet can hinder educational progress among students living in remote rural communities.
ex.zh: 無法充分使用穩定的互聯網，會阻礙偏遠農村地區學生的學業進步。

words.tip: hinder是使事情更困難，不一定像prevent那樣完全阻止。

ex.zh: 每次我打開櫥櫃，生鏽的合頁都會吱吱作響。

ex.en: The success of public transport reforms may hinge on reliable funding and sustained support from local residents.
ex.zh: 公共交通改革的成功可能取決於可靠的資金來源和當地居民的持續支持。

words.tip: hinge on 後接名詞或從句，表示“取決於”。

words.tip: 正式用語，常見於hitherto unknown等搭配。

col: a hive of activity｜繁忙的場所

ex.zh: 種豆子前，我們把菜地鋤了一遍。

ex.en: Farmers who hoe between crop rows can control weeds while reducing their dependence on chemical herbicides.
ex.zh: 在作物行間鋤地的農民可以控制雜草，同時減少對化學除草劑的依賴。

ex.zh: 建築工人使用專用設備安全吊起重物，以減輕身體負擔並減少工傷。

ex.zh: 養老照護機構中溫馨的氛圍可能讓老年人感到更舒適、更安心。

ex.zh: 負債累累的國家可能難以充分投資公共醫療和教育。

To compensate for loss or provide financial protection against it.

ex.en: The insurer agreed to indemnify us for the damage.
ex.zh: 保險公司同意賠償我們遭受的損失。

ex.en: Construction contracts often require companies to indemnify clients against financial losses caused by negligence.
ex.zh: 建築合同通常要求公司賠償客戶因疏忽而遭受的經濟損失。

indemnify someone for damage｜賠償某人的損害
words.tip: 法律正式用語：for接已受損害，against接防範風險。

ex.zh: 請將每個新段落的首行縮進。

ex.en: Students should learn to indent paragraphs consistently when formatting formal reports for their university courses.
ex.zh: 學生應學會在排版大學課程正式報告時，統一設置段落縮進。

ex.en: These dark clouds indicate that rain is coming.
ex.zh: 這些烏雲表明快要下雨了。

ex.en: Recent surveys indicate that affordable housing remains a major concern for young adults in urban areas.
ex.zh: 近期調查表明，經濟適用住房仍是城市年輕人十分關心的問題。

ex.en: Our cat remained indifferent to its expensive new toy.
ex.zh: 我們家的貓對昂貴的新玩具仍然毫無興趣。

ex.en: People may appear indifferent to environmental problems when they believe their individual actions cannot make a difference.
ex.zh: 當人們認為個人行動無法帶來改變時，可能會顯得對環境問題漠不關心。

words.tip: 常用be indifferent to；這裡的to是介詞。

Originating or living naturally in a place, rather than arriving later.

ex.en: These flowers are indigenous to the valley near our village.
ex.zh: 這些花原產於我們村莊附近的山谷。

ex.en: Protecting indigenous languages helps preserve cultural knowledge that has been passed down through many generations.
ex.zh: 保護原住民語言有助於保存世代相傳的文化知識。

col: indigenous to an area｜原產於某地區
words.tip: 常用indigenous to；修飾人群時常將首字母大寫。

憤憤不平的；憤慨的

Angry because something seems unfair or insulting.

ex.en: She was indignant when someone pushed ahead in the queue.
ex.zh: 有人插隊時，她感到憤憤不平。

ex.en: Residents were indignant about the council's decision to close their only public swimming pool.
ex.zh: 市政委員會決定關閉當地唯一的公共遊泳池，居民對此十分憤慨。

words.tip: 強調因不公或受辱而生氣，不泛指憤怒。

ex.en: The teacher gave each child an individual box of crayons.
ex.zh: 老師給每個孩子單獨發了一盒彩色蠟筆。

ex.en: Education systems should recognise individual learning needs rather than expect every student to progress at the same pace.
ex.zh: 教育體系應重視個人的學習需求，而不是指望每個學生都以相同的速度進步。

words.tip: 形容詞強調單個或個人；作可數名詞指一個人或個體。

ex.zh: 免費送貨這一優惠足以促使我們訂購那張沙發。

ex.en: Financial inducements may encourage households to install solar panels, reducing their dependence on fossil fuels.
ex.zh: 經濟激勵措施可能促使家庭安裝太陽能電池板，減少對化石燃料的依賴。

words.tip: 常指外部提供的獎勵或好處，後可接to do。

ex.zh: 我們的入職培訓包括參觀整個辦公室。

ex.en: A structured induction programme can help new employees understand workplace expectations and adapt to their roles.
ex.zh: 系統的入職培訓可以幫助新員工瞭解工作要求並適應崗位。

ex.zh: 我勤勞的鄰居每個週末都種菜、修傢俱。

ex.zh: 儘管勤奮的員工對生產效率貢獻很大，僱主也必須提供充分的培訓和合理的工作條件。

words.tip: industrious 指勤奮的；industrial 指工業的。

ex.zh: 交通這麼擁堵，延誤似乎不可避免。

ex.zh: 隨著工廠引入能更高效完成常規任務的機器，一些崗位流失可能難以避免。

ex.zh: 我們看著無法阻擋的潮水逐漸逼近沙堡。

ex.zh: 電力需求不可阻擋的增長凸顯了投資可再生能源的必要性。

words.tip: 側重趨勢或進程無法阻止，不只是“無情”。

ex.zh: 我們在火車站附近找到了一家價格實惠的咖啡館。

ex.en: Cycling offers an inexpensive alternative to driving and can help reduce traffic congestion in growing cities.
ex.zh: 騎自行車是駕車之外一種經濟實惠的選擇，也有助於緩解發展中城市的交通擁堵。

words.tip: 比cheap更中性，通常不暗示質量差。

嬰兒
嬰兒的；初期的
def: n a very young child (birth to 1 year) who has not yet begun to walk or talk
a baby or very young child
relating to babies or an early stage of development

ex.en: The infant slept peacefully in her father's arms.
ex.zh: 那個嬰兒在父親懷裡安靜地睡著。

ex.en: Access to clean water and basic healthcare is essential for reducing infant mortality in disadvantaged communities.
ex.zh: 獲得清潔飲水和基本醫療服務，對於降低弱勢社區的嬰兒死亡率至關重要。

words.tip: 比baby正式；infant mortality專指嬰兒死亡率。

步兵；步兵部隊
def: n. an army unit consisting of soldiers who fight on foot
soldiers trained to fight on foot

ex.en: The infantry marched past our village early this morning.
ex.zh: 今天一大早，步兵部隊行軍經過了我們的村莊。

ex.en: Although military technology has changed considerably, infantry still play an important role in many countries' defence forces.
ex.zh: 儘管軍事技術發生了巨大變化，步兵在許多國家的國防力量中仍發揮著重要作用。

words.tip: 集合名詞，指步兵整體，不用an infantry指一個人。

v. contaminate with a disease or microorganism
v. corrupt with ideas or an ideology

ex.en: One sick rabbit can infect the others in its cage.
ex.zh: 一隻生病的兔子可能傳染同籠的其他兔子。

ex.en: Viruses can infect vulnerable patients more easily when hospitals lack effective hygiene measures and adequate ventilation.
ex.zh: 如果醫院缺乏有效的衛生措施和充分的通風，病毒就更容易感染身體脆弱的患者。

col: infect someone with a virus｜使某人感染病毒
words.tip: 常用infect someone with a virus，表示使某人感染病毒。

n. (medicine) the invasion of the body by pathogenic microorganisms and their multiplication which can lead to tissue damage and disease

ex.en: The doctor checked my sore throat for signs of infection.
ex.zh: 醫生檢查了我疼痛的喉嚨，看是否有感染跡象。

ex.en: Improved sanitation can reduce the risk of infection, particularly in communities with limited access to clean water.
ex.zh: 改善衛生條件可以降低感染風險，尤其是在難以獲得潔淨水的社區。

words.tip: infection既可指感染過程，也可指一次具體感染。

傳染性的
有感染力的

a. easily spread; children catch it from their elders"- Bertrand Russell
a. of or relating to infection

ex.zh: 他富有感染力的笑聲很快讓桌邊的每個人都笑了起來。

ex.en: Improved sanitation and access to clean water are essential for preventing infectious diseases in densely populated communities.
ex.zh: 改善衛生條件並保障清潔用水，對預防人口密集社區的傳染病至關重要。

words.tip: infectious表示有傳染性；infected表示已被感染。

ex.zh: 從她沾滿泥土的鞋子，我推斷她剛才在做園藝活。

ex.en: Researchers cannot infer that smaller classes improve learning without examining other factors affecting student performance.
ex.zh: 研究人員如果不考察影響學生表現的其他因素，就不能推斷小班教學能改善學習效果。

ex.zh: 那個便宜包摸起來不如皮包好。

ex.en: Schools in disadvantaged areas should not receive inferior equipment simply because local funding is limited.
ex.zh: 弱勢地區的學校不應僅因當地資金有限就獲得較差的設備。

ex.zh: 老鼠可能在維護不善的住房中大量出沒，給人口密集地區的居民帶來嚴重健康風險。

ex.zh: 暴風雨嚴重損壞了我們花園的圍欄。

ex.en: Unregulated industrial activity can inflict lasting damage on ecosystems and threaten the livelihoods of nearby communities.

ex.zh: 姐姐對我有很大的影響。

ex.zh: 廣告會影響兒童的食物偏好，因此負責任的營銷對公眾健康尤為重要。

ex.zh: 她的祖父曾是村裡一位很有影響力的教師。

ex.zh: 科學顧問可以在制定公共衛生和環境保護政策方面發揮重要影響。

words.tip: 告知某人某事用inform sb of/about sth。

ex.en: He built an ingenious watering system from old bottles.
ex.zh: 他用舊瓶子做了一套巧妙的澆水裝置。

ex.zh: 巧妙的設計可以幫助建築師在小塊土地上建造舒適住宅，同時不犧牲自然採光。

ex.zh: 莉娜巧妙地把舊板條箱改成了架子。

ex.zh: 人類的巧思能幫助社區利用當地材料，開發經濟實惠的缺水應對方案。

ex.zh: 她天真坦率的提問讓餐桌旁的每個人都笑了。

ex.zh: 我們家附近的岩石潮池裡棲息著小螃蟹。

ex.zh: 即使是簡單的家居維修也有一些固有風險。

ex.zh: 萊拉從祖母那裡繼承了一間小屋。

ex.zh: 除非各國政府採取果斷措施減少汙染，否則後代可能要接手嚴重的環境問題。

ex.zh: 寒冷天氣會抑制這些植物的生長。

ex.zh: 害怕犯錯可能使學生不敢積極參與課堂討論和合作任務。

ex.zh: 看到價格後，我最初的興奮消退了。

ex.zh: 雖然太陽能電池板的初期費用較高，但從長遠看，家庭可能節省開支。

ex.zh: 地方政府應啟動相關項目，鼓勵居民更有效地回收生活垃圾。

ex.zh: 每位服刑人員都可以從監獄圖書館借書。

ex.en: Providing inmates with vocational training may improve their employment prospects and reduce the risk of reoffending.
ex.zh: 為服刑人員提供職業培訓可能改善其就業前景，降低再次犯罪的風險。

ex.zh: 她的問題似乎無傷大雅，所以我毫不猶豫地回答了。

ex.en: Seemingly innocuous household products can damage aquatic ecosystems when large quantities enter rivers through wastewater.
ex.zh: 看似無害的家用產品如果隨廢水大量進入河流，也可能破壞水生生態系統。

ex.zh: 批評者認為這項提案荒唐至極，因為其巨大成本會超過任何潛在收益。

ex.zh: 學校應將數字工具融入課堂活動，同時確保所有學生都能平等使用。

ex.zh: 她歸還了撿到的錢，體現了誠實正直的品質。

ex.zh: 我們匆忙趕往車站時，雨下得更大了。

ex.zh: 氣溫上升可能加劇長期遭受乾旱地區的缺水問題。

Stopping and starting repeatedly rather than continuing without a break.

ex.en: Intermittent rain kept us running indoors throughout the afternoon.
ex.zh: 整個下午，斷斷續續的雨讓我們不時跑回屋裡。

ex.en: Intermittent internet access can prevent rural students from participating fully in online learning programmes.
ex.zh: 網絡連接時斷時續，會妨礙農村學生充分參與在線學習課程。

words.tip: 強調時停時續，不一定按固定週期發生。

To explain or understand the meaning of something

ex.en: I interpreted her smile as permission to sit down.
ex.zh: 我把她的微笑理解為允許我坐下。

ex.en: Researchers must interpret survey results carefully because cultural differences may influence how participants understand the questions.
ex.zh: 研究人員必須謹慎解讀調查結果，因為文化差異可能影響參與者對問題的理解。

def: n. a signal that temporarily stops the execution of a program so that another procedure can be carried out
v. make a break in
v. destroy the peace or tranquility of

ex.en: Please don't interrupt me while I explain the rules.
ex.zh: 我講解規則時，請不要打斷我。

ex.en: Frequent phone notifications can interrupt students' concentration and reduce the amount they learn during independent study.
ex.zh: 頻繁的手機通知會打斷學生的注意力，減少他們在自主學習中的收穫。

col: interrupt the flow｜打斷連貫過程
words.tip: interrupt指中途打斷；disrupt側重擾亂正常進程。

tr: n. 打擾, 中斷, 障礙物
[醫] 間斷, 阻斷, 中止
打斷；中斷
def: n. some abrupt occurrence that interrupts an ongoing activity
Something that briefly stops an activity, conversation, or continuous process.

ex.en: Sorry for the interruption, but your taxi is here.
ex.zh: 抱歉打斷一下，不過你的出租車到了。

ex.en: Frequent interruptions in open offices can reduce concentration and make complex tasks take longer to complete.
ex.zh: 開放式辦公室中頻繁的干擾可能降低注意力，使複雜任務需要更長時間才能完成。

words.tip: 一次打斷可數；without interruption表示不間斷。

tr: vt. 貫穿, 橫穿
vi. 交錯, 相交

tr: vt. 散佈, 點綴
穿插；點綴；散佈
def: v. place at intervals in or among
v. introduce one's writing or speech with certain expressions
to place things among others at intervals

ex.en: She interspersed bright flowers among the herbs on her balcony.
ex.zh: 她在陽臺的香草植物之間點綴了鮮豔的花朵。

ex.en: Teachers can intersperse short discussions throughout lectures to maintain attention and encourage students to participate.
ex.zh: 教師可以在講課過程中穿插簡短討論，以保持學生的注意力並鼓勵參與。

[法] 告知, 通知, 暗示
暗示；間接透露
def: n an indirect suggestion
n a slight suggestion or vague understanding
An indirect suggestion or indication of something.

ex.en: His sudden silence gave us an intimation of trouble.
ex.zh: 他突然沉默，讓我們隱約感到出了問題。

ex.en: The minister's remarks offered the first intimation that funding for public transport might increase.
ex.zh: 部長的講話首次暗示，公共交通資金可能會增加。

col: an intimation of trouble｜麻煩的徵兆
words.tip: 別與intimacy（親密）混淆；常接of或that從句。

tr: vt. 威脅, 恐嚇

恐嚇；威脅
使膽怯；使失去信心
def: v. make timid or fearful
v. to compel or deter by or as if by threats
To frighten someone, often to make them obey

ex.en: The large audience intimidated her before her first performance.
ex.zh: 首次演出前，龐大的觀眾群讓她有些膽怯。

ex.en: Employers should never intimidate workers into accepting unsafe conditions or giving up their legal rights.
ex.zh: 僱主絕不應脅迫員工接受不安全的工作條件或放棄合法權利。

col: intimidate someone into doing something｜脅迫某人做某事
words.tip: intimidate sb into doing sth表示脅迫某人做某事。

tr: vt. 使陶醉, 使喝醉

v. have an intoxicating effect on, of a drug

def: a. not tractable; difficult to manage or mold

激起好奇心；引起興趣
陰謀；密謀
def: n. a crafty and involved plot to achieve your (usually sinister) ends
n. a clandestine love affair
v. cause to be interested or curious

ex.en: The locked wooden box intrigued everyone in the room.
ex.zh: 那個上鎖的木盒引起了屋裡所有人的好奇。

ex.en: Unexplained archaeological discoveries continue to intrigue researchers and encourage further investigation into the lives of ancient communities.
ex.zh: 尚未得到解釋的考古發現持續引起研究者的興趣，推動他們進一步探索古代社群的生活。

col: a web of intrigue｜錯綜複雜的陰謀
words.tip: 激起興趣時是及物動詞；常用 be intrigued by。

[醫] 內部的, 內在的
固有的；內在的

s. situated within or belonging solely to the organ or body part on which it acts
Belonging naturally to something, rather than coming from outside

ex.en: She values the intrinsic beauty of untreated wood.
ex.zh: 她欣賞未經加工的木材本身的美。

ex.en: Schools should encourage intrinsic motivation by helping students enjoy learning rather than focusing solely on external rewards.
ex.zh: 學校應幫助學生享受學習，培養內在動力，而不是隻關注外部獎勵。

words.tip: intrinsic to表示“……所固有的”。

大量湧入

v. occupy in large numbers or live on a host
v. penetrate or assault, in a harmful or injurious way

ex.en: Ants invaded our kitchen after we left cake out.
ex.zh: 我們把蛋糕放在外面後，螞蟻大批湧進了廚房。

ex.en: Some monitoring technologies can invade people's privacy, even when they are introduced to improve public safety.
ex.zh: 某些監控技術即使是為改善公共安全而引入的，也可能侵犯人們的隱私。

col: invade a country｜入侵一個國家
invade someone's privacy｜侵犯某人的隱私
invade personal space｜侵入個人空間
words.tip: 及物動詞，直接接賓語；名詞形式是invasion。

使失效；使作廢
使不能成立

v. show to be invalid
v. take away the legal force of or render ineffective

ex.en: Opening the device yourself may invalidate its warranty.
ex.zh: 自行拆開這臺設備可能會使保修失效。

ex.en: A sample that excludes older adults may invalidate conclusions about the health needs of the wider population.
ex.zh: 如果樣本排除了老年人，關於整體人口健康需求的結論就可能無法成立。

col: invalidate the results｜使結果失去效力
words.tip: 可指合同等正式失效，也可指證據使結論不能成立。

v speak against in an impassioned manner

tr: vt. 誘騙；誘使

[經] 發明
發明物
發明；創造
虛構的事；編造
def: n. the creation of something in the mind
n. a creation (a new device or process) resulting from study and experimentation
n. the act of inventing

ex.en: Her latest invention waters the plants while she is away.
ex.zh: 她最新的發明能在她外出時給植物澆水。

ex.en: The invention of affordable water filters has improved public health in communities with limited access to clean water.
ex.zh: 價格低廉的濾水器的發明改善了難以獲得清潔用水的社區的公共衛生狀況。

words.tip: invention創造原本沒有的東西；discovery發現已有事物。

庫存；存貨
def: n. a detailed list of all the items in stock
n. (accounting) the value of a firm's current assets including raw materials and work in progress and finished goods
n. making an itemized list of merchandise or supplies on hand

ex.en: We made an inventory of everything in the garage.
ex.zh: 我們把車庫裡的所有東西列成了清單。

ex.en: Digital systems help retailers manage inventory more efficiently, reducing waste and preventing shortages of essential products.
ex.zh: 數字系統幫助零售商更高效地管理庫存，減少浪費並防止必需品短缺。

words.tip: 表示庫存時多見於美式英語，英式常用stock。

tr: a. 倒轉的, 相反的
n. 反向, 反面

反向的；成反比的
相反事物；逆運算
def: n. something inverted in sequence or character or effect
s. reversed (turned backward) in order or nature or effect
a. opposite in nature or effect or relation to another quantity

ex.en: Our free time and workload have an inverse relationship.
ex.zh: 我們的空閒時間與工作量呈反向關係。

ex.en: The study found an inverse relationship between regular physical activity and reported stress levels among office workers.
ex.zh: 研究發現，上班族的規律運動量與其報告的壓力水平呈負相關。

words.tip: inverse relationship指一方增加時另一方減少。

tr: v. 調查, 審查
調查；查明
研究；探究
def: v. investigate scientifically
v. conduct an inquiry or investigation of
To examine facts carefully to discover what happened or why.

ex.en: A plumber came to investigate the strange noise upstairs.
ex.zh: 一位水管工來查明樓上怪聲的原因。

ex.en: Researchers are investigating how access to green spaces affects the mental health of urban residents.
ex.zh: 研究人員正在探究接觸綠地如何影響城市居民的心理健康。

words.tip: 直接接調查對象：investigate the problem，不加into。

tr: a. 根深的, 成癖的, 積習的

積習難改的；成癖的
def: s habitual
r in a habitual and longstanding manner
Having a long-established habit that is unlikely to change.

ex.en: My uncle is an inveterate collector of old maps.
ex.zh: 我叔叔收藏舊地圖成癖。

ex.en: Inveterate car users may resist public transport initiatives unless services become substantially more convenient and reliable.
ex.zh: 除非服務變得便捷可靠得多，否則長期習慣開車的人可能會牴觸推廣公共交通的舉措。

col: inveterate traveller｜常年熱衷旅行的人
words.tip: 通常置於名詞前，強調長期習慣難以改變。

s must be kept sacred

v. 開發票, 記清單
發票；付款清單
向……開具發票
def: v. send an bill to
a document listing goods or services and the payment required
to send someone a document requesting payment for goods or services

ex.en: The plumber emailed an invoice after fixing our sink.
ex.zh: 水管工修好我們的水槽後，通過電子郵件發來了付款清單。

ex.en: Small businesses benefit from digital systems that track each invoice and remind customers when payments are due.
ex.zh: 小企業可以從追蹤每張發票並提醒客戶按時付款的數字系統中受益。

col: pay an invoice｜支付發票款項
an outstanding invoice｜尚未結清的發票
invoice someone for something｜就某項費用向某人開票
words.tip: invoice 通常用於要求付款；receipt 是已付款的收據。

[計] 調用; 請求
def: v. cite as an authority; resort to

a. controlled by the autonomic nervous system; without conscious control

使參與
def: v. connect closely and often incriminatingly
v. engage as a participant
v. contain as a part

ex.en: My new job involves talking to customers all day.
ex.zh: 我的新工作需要整天與顧客交談。

ex.en: Local authorities should involve residents in planning decisions to ensure that new developments meet community needs.
ex.zh: 地方政府應讓居民參與規劃決策，確保新的開發項目滿足社區需求。

tr: n. 彩虹色

tr: vt. 使厭倦, 使苦惱

ex.en: The irony is that our swimming lesson was cancelled by rain.
ex.zh: 諷刺的是，我們的游泳課竟因下雨而取消了。

ex.en: There is considerable irony in promoting environmental awareness through disposable products that create additional waste.
ex.zh: 通過製造更多垃圾的一次性產品來宣傳環保意識，頗具諷刺意味。

v. expose to radiation
