n. a territory surrendered by Turkey or Germany after World War I and put under the tutelage of some other European power until they are able to stand by themselves
n. the commission that is given to a government and its policies through an electoral victory

tr: vt. 亂砍, 損壞, 軋布
n. 軋布機
def: n. clothes dryer for drying and ironing laundry by passing it between two heavy heated rollers
v. press with a mangle
v. alter so as to make unrecognizable

tr: n. 狂躁, 熱衷, 狂熱
[醫] 躁狂, 狂
狂熱；痴迷
躁狂
def: n. an irrational but irresistible motive for a belief or action
n. a mood disorder; an affective disorder in which the victim tends to respond excessively and sometimes violently
an unusually strong enthusiasm for an activity or object

ex.en: A mania for collecting toy trains swept our neighbourhood.
ex.zh: 收集玩具火車的熱潮席捲了我們社區。

ex.en: During episodes of mania, individuals may need professional support to manage sleep disruption and impulsive behaviour.
ex.zh: 在躁狂發作期間，患者可能需要專業支持來應對睡眠紊亂和衝動行為。

col: an episode of mania｜一次躁狂發作
words.tip: 日常可指狂熱；醫學上的躁狂不等於普通興奮。

tr: n. 宣言, 聲明
宣言；政綱
def: n. a public declaration of intentions (as issued by a political party or government)
A public statement of a group's beliefs, aims, and planned actions.

ex.en: Our club published a manifesto calling for cleaner parks.
ex.zh: 我們俱樂部發表了一份宣言，呼籲讓公園更清潔。

ex.en: The party's manifesto promises greater investment in public transport to reduce congestion in major cities.
ex.zh: 該黨的政綱承諾加大公共交通投入，以緩解大城市的交通擁堵。

words.tip: 複數可用manifestos或manifestoes。

tr: vt. 操縱, 利用, 操作, 巧妙地處理, 假造
操縱；擺佈
熟練操作；處理
def: v. influence or control shrewdly or deviously
v. hold something in one's hands and move it
v. control (others or oneself) or influence skillfully, usually to one's advantage

ex.en: She tried to manipulate her brother into doing the dishes.
ex.zh: 她試圖用手段讓弟弟去洗碗。

ex.en: Online platforms can manipulate consumer choices by selectively displaying products and controlling access to information.
ex.zh: 網絡平臺可以通過選擇性展示商品和控制信息獲取來操縱消費者的選擇。

col: manipulate someone into doing something｜操縱某人做某事
words.tip: 操縱人做某事用manipulate sb into doing。

tr: n. 大廈, 宅邸
豪宅；大宅邸
def: n. a large and imposing house
A very large, impressive house.

ex.en: An enormous mansion stood behind the tall iron gates.
ex.zh: 高高的鐵門後矗立著一座巨大的宅邸。

ex.en: The historic mansion has been converted into a museum to preserve the region's cultural heritage.
ex.zh: 這座歷史悠久的宅邸已被改建為博物館，以保護當地的文化遺產。

col: a sprawling mansion｜佔地廣闊的豪宅
words.tip: 通常指大型豪宅，不是普通辦公大廈。

tr: n. 肥料, 糞肥
vt. 施肥於
糞肥
給土地施糞肥
def: n. any animal or plant material used to fertilize land especially animal excreta usually with litter material
v. spread manure, as for fertilization
Animal waste used to improve soil and help plants grow.

ex.en: The farmer spread manure around the young apple trees.
ex.zh: 農民在幼小的蘋果樹周圍撒上糞肥。

ex.en: Using manure can improve soil fertility, but excessive application may pollute nearby rivers and groundwater.
ex.zh: 施用糞肥可以提高土壤肥力，但過量施用可能汙染附近河流和地下水。

words.tip: 名詞通常不可數；fertilizer泛指肥料，範圍更廣。

tr: n. 楓, 楓木, 淡棕色
[機] 楓木
def: n. wood of any of various maple trees; especially the hard close-grained wood of the sugar maple; used especially for furniture and flooring
n. any of numerous trees or shrubs of the genus Acer bearing winged seeds in pairs; north temperate zone

tr: vt. 損毀, 損傷, 糟蹋
n. 三月
def: v. make imperfect

tr: v. 劫掠, 掠奪, 襲擊
n. 劫掠, 掠奪, 襲擊
def: v. raid and rove in search of booty

tr: n. 艦隊, 水兵, 海景畫
a. 海的, 海產的, 海底的, 船舶的, 海運的
海洋的；海生的
海運的；船舶的
海軍陸戰隊員
def: n. a member of the United States Marine Corps
n. a soldier who serves both on shipboard and on land
a. of or relating to the sea

ex.en: We watched a documentary about marine life last night.
ex.zh: 我們昨晚看了一部關於海洋生物的紀錄片。

ex.en: Plastic pollution threatens marine ecosystems and reduces the income of communities that depend on fishing.
ex.zh: 塑料汙染威脅海洋生態系統，並減少依靠捕魚為生的社區的收入。

words.tip: marine側重海洋；海軍的通常用naval。

tr: n. 水手
海員；水手
def: n. a man who serves as a sailor
Someone who sails or works on a ship at sea.

ex.en: The experienced mariner guided our boat safely into harbour.
ex.zh: 那位經驗豐富的海員引導我們的船安全駛入港口。

ex.en: Before modern navigation systems existed, mariners relied on stars and coastal landmarks to determine their position.
ex.zh: 在現代導航系統出現之前，海員依靠星辰和海岸地標確定位置。

col: an experienced mariner｜經驗豐富的海員
a master mariner｜持證遠洋船長
words.tip: 比sailor正式，常見於航海或歷史語境。

tr: n. 髓, 骨髓, 精華, 活力, 配偶
[醫] 髓(尤指骨髓)
def: n. the fatty network of connective tissue that fills the cavities of bones
n. any of various squash plants grown for their elongated fruit with smooth dark green skin and whitish flesh
n. very tender and very nutritious tissue from marrowbones

tr: n. 元帥, 陸空軍高級將官, 典禮官, 執法官
vt. 整理, 引領, 統率
vi. 排列, 各就各位
組織；調集；整理
活動秩序員
def: n. a law officer having duties similar to those of a sheriff in carrying out the judgments of a court of law
n. (in some countries) a military officer of highest rank
v. place in proper rank

ex.en: A volunteer marshalled the runners into a neat line.
ex.zh: 一名志願者把跑步者組織成了整齊的一隊。

ex.en: Governments must marshal resources effectively to provide emergency housing for communities affected by severe flooding.
ex.zh: 政府必須有效調集資源，為遭受嚴重洪災的社區提供應急住房。

words.tip: 英式過去式marshalled，美式marshaled；勿混淆martial。

tr: n. 有袋類動物
a. 有袋的, 袋狀的
def: n. mammals of which the females have a pouch (the marsupium) containing the teats where the young are fed and carried
a. of or relating to the marsupials

tr: a. 戰爭的, 軍事的, 尚武的, 威武的
[醫] 含鐵的
軍事的；戰爭的
def: n. Roman poet noted for epigrams (first century BC)
s. of or relating to the armed forces
Related to war, soldiers, or military life.

ex.en: The band played martial music as soldiers marched past.
ex.zh: 士兵列隊走過時，樂隊奏起了軍樂。

ex.en: Although martial arts originated as fighting techniques, many people now practise them for fitness and self-discipline.
ex.zh: 雖然武術起源於格鬥技巧，如今許多人練習武術是為了健身和培養自律。

words.tip: martial是軍事的；marital是婚姻的，勿混。

tr: n. 烈士, 受苦者, 受難者
vt. 使成為烈士, 使受苦
def: n. one who suffers for the sake of principle
n. one who voluntarily suffers death as the penalty for refusing to renounce their religion
v. kill as a martyr

tr: n. 奇異事物, 罕見例子
vt. 驚異於
vi. 驚異
令人驚歎的人或事物
感到驚歎
def: v. express astonishment or surprise about something
Someone or something that causes great admiration or surprise
To feel great surprise or admiration

ex.en: We marvelled at the tiny bird's beautifully woven nest.
ex.zh: 那隻小鳥精巧編織的巢讓我們驚歎不已。

ex.en: The new bridge is an engineering marvel that connects isolated communities and improves access to essential services.
ex.zh: 這座新橋是一項工程奇蹟，連接了偏遠社區，並讓居民更方便地獲得基本服務。

col: a marvel of nature｜自然奇觀
words.tip: 動詞常接at；英式過去式marvelled，美式marveled。

tr: n. 碎麥芽, 飼料, 糊狀物
vt. 調情, 搗碎
def: n. a mixture of mashed malt grains and hot water; used in brewing
n. mixture of ground animal feeds

tr: n. 化裝舞會, 偽裝
vi. 參加化裝舞會, 偽裝, 假裝
def: n. a party of guests wearing costumes and masks
n. making a false outward show
v. take part in a masquerade

tr: n. 大屠殺
vt. 大屠殺, 殘殺
大屠殺
屠殺
def: v. kill a large number of people indiscriminately
The deliberate killing of many people, especially those unable to defend themselves.
To deliberately kill many people, especially those unable to defend themselves.

ex.en: We visited a memorial to victims of the massacre.
ex.zh: 我們參觀了一座紀念大屠殺遇難者的紀念碑。

ex.en: Teaching about a historical massacre requires sensitivity, reliable evidence, and respect for victims and their communities.
ex.zh: 講授歷史上的大屠殺事件，需要謹慎體察、可靠證據，以及對遇難者及其群體的尊重。

col: a brutal massacre｜殘酷的大屠殺
commemorate a massacre｜紀念大屠殺事件
words.tip: 指大規模殘殺，語氣極重；勿用於一般傷亡事件。

tr: a. 大而重的, 寬大的, 宏偉的
[醫] 大塊的, 整塊的, 大量的
巨大的；厚重的
大量的；程度極大的
def: s. imposing in size or bulk or solidity
s. being the same substance throughout
s. imposing in scale or scope or degree or power

ex.en: A massive oak tree shades our entire garden.
ex.zh: 一棵巨大的橡樹為我們整個花園遮陰。

ex.en: The transition to renewable energy requires massive investment in infrastructure and training for workers.
ex.zh: 向可再生能源轉型需要在基礎設施和工人培訓方面投入大量資金。

words.tip: 既可形容體積巨大，也可形容投入或變化程度極大。

tr: n. 桅, 桅杆, 杆
vt. 裝桅杆於
桅杆
天線塔；天線杆
def: n. a vertical spar for supporting sails
n. nuts of forest trees (as beechnuts and acorns) accumulated on the ground
n. nuts of forest trees used as feed for swine

ex.en: A white sail fluttered high on the wooden mast.
ex.zh: 一面白帆在木桅杆高處迎風飄動。

ex.en: Installing a new communications mast could improve mobile coverage in remote villages and support local businesses.
ex.zh: 安裝新的通信塔可以改善偏遠村莊的移動通信覆蓋，並支持當地企業發展。

words.tip: 核心義是支撐帆的桅杆，也可指支撐天線的高杆。

tr: v. 咀嚼
def: v. grind and knead

tr: n. 墊, 叢, 襯邊
a. 粗糙的, 無光澤的
vi. 糾纏在一起
vt. 鋪席於...上, 使無光澤, 使纏結
墊子；席子
def: n. a thick flat pad used as a floor covering
n. mounting consisting of a border or background for a picture
n. sports equipment consisting of a piece of thick padding on the floor for gymnastic sports

ex.en: Please wipe your shoes on the mat before entering.
ex.zh: 進門前請在墊子上擦擦鞋。

ex.en: Placing a rubber mat near each entrance can help prevent slips in busy public buildings.
ex.zh: 在每個入口附近放置橡膠墊，有助於防止人們在繁忙的公共建築內滑倒。

words.tip: mat通常是小塊功能性墊子，不等同於carpet。

tr: vt. 賦予實質, 使體現, 物質化
vi. 成有形, 體現, 實現
實現；成為現實
突然出現
def: v come into being; become reality
To happen or become real after being expected or planned.
To appear suddenly or unexpectedly.

ex.en: Our weekend trip never materialized because everyone was too busy.
ex.zh: 大家都太忙，我們的週末旅行最終沒能成行。

ex.en: The promised economic benefits may not materialize unless governments also invest in education and transport.
ex.zh: 除非政府也投資教育和交通，否則承諾的經濟效益可能無法實現。

words.tip: 常作不及物動詞，指計劃實現；英式也寫materialise。

tr: vt. 准許入學, 錄取
vi. 入學, 進大學
n. 獲准入學者
def: n. someone who has been admitted to a college or university
v. enroll as a student

tr: a. 表面粗糙的
n. 無光粗糙層, 冰銅
def: n. a mixture of sulfides that forms when sulfide metal ores are smelted

tr: n. 床墊, 空氣墊, 沉床
[醫] 褥子, 床墊
def: n. a large thick pad filled with resilient material and often incorporating coiled springs, used as a bed or part of a bed

tr: a. 成熟的, 到期的, 充分考慮的
vt. 使成熟
vi. 成熟, 到期
成熟的；明事理的
發育完全的；成年的
def: v. develop and reach maturity; undergo maturation
v. develop and work out fully in one's mind
v. become due for repayment

ex.en: Leila gave a mature response when her plans changed.
ex.zh: 計劃改變時，萊拉作出了成熟理智的回應。

ex.en: Living independently can help young adults mature as they learn to manage money and resolve everyday problems.
ex.zh: 獨立生活能幫助年輕人在學習理財和解決日常問題的過程中變得成熟。

col: a mature student｜成年後重返校園的學生
words.tip: 既可指身體發育成熟，也可指處事明智。

tr: n. 大槌
vt. 打傷, 粗手粗腳地擺弄, 抨擊
def: n. a heavy long-handled hammer used to drive stakes or wedges
v. split (wood) with a maul and wedges
v. injure badly by beating

tr: vi. 嘮叨地講, 徘徊
def: v. wander aimlessly

tr: a. 淡而無味的, 令人作嘔的, 感傷的
def: s effusively or insincerely emotional

tr: n. 迷宮, 迷惘
vt. 使迷惘, 使混亂, 迷失
def: n. complex system of paths or tunnels in which it is easy to get lost

tr: a. 低劣的, 卑賤的, 簡陋的, 吝嗇的, 慚愧的, 平均的, 中間的, 普通的
vt. 意謂, 想要, 意欲, 預定
vi. 用意, 有意義
n. 平均數, 中間, 中庸
意思是；意味著；打算
def: n. an average of n numbers computed by adding some function of the numbers and dividing by some function of n
v. mean or intend to express or convey
v. denote or connote

ex.en: I didn't mean to leave you waiting outside.
ex.zh: 我不是故意讓你在外面等著的。

ex.en: Higher energy prices may mean that low-income households have less money available for other essential needs.
ex.zh: 能源價格上漲可能意味著低收入家庭可用於其他基本需求的錢會更少。

col: mean to do something｜打算做某事
mean doing something｜意味著做某事
be mean to someone｜對某人刻薄
words.tip: mean to do是“打算做”；mean doing是“意味著做”。

tr: n. (河流的)蜿蜒, 漫步, 迂迴旅行
vi. 蜿蜒流動, 漫步
vt. 使蜿蜒曲折
def: n. a bend or curve, as in a stream or river

tr: a. 患麻疹的
[醫] 米珠的, 含囊尾蚴的
def: s. contemptibly small in amount

tr: a. 整齊的, 慎重的, 基於標準的
def: s. the rhythmic arrangement of syllables

tr: n. 機械, 機構, 結構, 機理, 技巧
[化] 機理; 歷程; 機構
機制；運作方式
機械裝置；機械結構
def: n. the atomic process that occurs during a chemical reaction
n. the technical aspects of doing something
n. a natural object resembling a machine in structure or function

ex.en: The club needs a fair mechanism for resolving disputes.
ex.zh: 俱樂部需要一個公平的爭議解決機制。

ex.en: Governments should establish effective monitoring mechanisms to ensure that environmental regulations are consistently enforced across industries.
ex.zh: 政府應建立有效的監督機制，確保各行業始終貫徹執行環境法規。

words.tip: mechanism for doing表示“做某事的機制或辦法”。

tr: n. 獎牌, 勳章
vt. 授勳予
獎牌；勳章
def: n an award for winning a championship or commemorating some other event
A metal award given for achievement, service, or bravery.

ex.en: She proudly showed us her first swimming medal.
ex.zh: 她自豪地向我們展示了她的第一枚游泳獎牌。

ex.en: Winning an international medal can encourage young athletes to pursue sport as a professional career.
ex.zh: 贏得國際賽事獎牌能鼓勵年輕運動員將體育作為職業來追求。

words.tip: medal是獎牌；metal是金屬，注意拼寫區別。

tr: vi. 干涉, 干預, 擅自摸弄
[法] 干預, 插手, 弄亂
干涉；管閒事
def: v. intrude in other people's affairs or business; interfere unwantedly
Interfere in other people's affairs without being invited.

ex.en: Please don't meddle in how I arrange my room.
ex.zh: 請別干涉我如何佈置自己的房間。

ex.en: Parents who constantly meddle in their children's decisions may prevent them from developing confidence and independence.
ex.zh: 不斷干涉孩子決定的父母可能會阻礙他們培養自信和獨立性。

col: meddle in someone's affairs｜干涉某人的私事
meddle with something｜擅自擺弄某物
words.tip: 常接in表示干涉事務；接with表示擅自擺弄。

tr: vt. 用藥治療
[醫] 用藥治療, 投藥, 加藥, 使含藥
def: v. impregnate with a medicinal substance
v. treat medicinally, treat with medicine

tr: a. 中古的, 中世紀的
中世紀的
def: a. relating to or belonging to the Middle Ages
s. as if belonging to the Middle Ages; old-fashioned and unenlightened
relating to European history from about AD 500 to 1500

ex.en: We explored a medieval castle during our weekend trip.
ex.zh: 我們在週末旅行中游覽了一座中世紀城堡。

ex.en: Preserving medieval buildings allows modern communities to understand how earlier generations lived, worked, and organised their societies.
ex.zh: 保護中世紀建築能讓現代社區瞭解前人如何生活、工作及組織社會。

words.tip: 通常指歐洲約公元500至1500年的中世紀。

tr: n. 沉思, 冥想
冥想；靜坐
沉思；深思
def: n. continuous and profound contemplation or musing on a subject or series of subjects of a deep or abstruse nature
n. (religion) contemplation of spiritual matters (usually on religious or philosophical subjects)
The practice of focusing attention to calm and train the mind.

ex.en: Ten minutes of meditation helps me relax before bed.
ex.zh: 睡前冥想十分鐘能幫助我放鬆。

ex.en: Some schools offer meditation sessions to help students manage stress and improve their ability to concentrate.
ex.zh: 一些學校開設冥想課程，幫助學生緩解壓力並提高專注力。

words.tip: 指冥想練習時通常不可數；meditation on可指對某事的沉思。

tr: a. 溫順的, 逆來順受的
溫順的；逆來順受的
def: s. humble in spirit or manner; suggesting retiring mildness or even cowed submissiveness
s. very docile
s. evidencing little spirit or courage; overly submissive or compliant

ex.en: He gave a meek nod and stepped aside.
ex.zh: 他順從地點了點頭，退到一旁。

ex.en: Students who seem meek in class may express strong opinions when given a supportive discussion environment.
ex.zh: 課堂上看似溫順的學生，在得到支持的討論環境中也可能表達堅定的觀點。

words.tip: 常暗含不敢反抗，不等同於褒義的 humble。

tr: v. 混合, 合併
def: v. announce for a score; of cards in a card game

tr: a. 加了蜜糖的, 甜蜜的, 甜美的, 流暢的
def: s pleasing to the ear

tr: n. 瓜, 甜瓜, 紅利, 贓物
[化] 三聚二氰亞胺
甜瓜
def: n. any of numerous fruits of the gourd family having a hard rind and sweet juicy flesh
n. any of various fruit of cucurbitaceous vines including: muskmelons; watermelons; cantaloupes; cucumbers
A large round fruit with thick skin and sweet, juicy flesh.

ex.en: She sliced a ripe melon for our picnic.
ex.zh: 她切了一個熟甜瓜，供我們野餐時吃。

ex.en: Farmers growing melons in dry regions often use efficient irrigation systems to reduce water consumption.
ex.zh: 乾旱地區種植甜瓜的農民常使用高效灌溉系統來減少用水量。

col: a slice of melon｜一片甜瓜
words.tip: melon泛指甜瓜類；watermelon專指西瓜。

tr: n. 薄膜, 膜, 羊皮紙

ex.zh: 教孩子修補衣物可以減少紡織廢料，並培養更負責任的消費態度。

ex.en: Some microbes help turn fresh milk into thick yoghurt.
ex.zh: 有些微生物能幫助把鮮奶變成濃稠的酸奶。

ex.en: Soil microbes play an essential role in recycling nutrients and maintaining the fertility of agricultural land.
ex.zh: 土壤微生物在養分循環和維持農田肥力方面發揮著關鍵作用。

A person's appearance or manner, especially showing mood or character.

ex.en: Her cheerful mien brightened the room as she entered.
ex.zh: 她走進來時，愉快的神情讓整個房間都明朗起來。

ex.en: Despite his stern mien, the headteacher encouraged students to discuss their concerns openly and without fear.
ex.zh: 儘管校長神情嚴肅，他仍鼓勵學生無所畏懼地坦誠討論自己的顧慮。

Very strong, powerful, or large.

ex.en: A mighty oak stood in the middle of the field.
ex.zh: 田野中央矗立著一棵高大的橡樹。

ex.en: Although mighty rivers provide valuable renewable energy, building large dams can seriously disrupt surrounding ecosystems.
ex.zh: 儘管大河能提供寶貴的可再生能源，修建大型水壩仍可能嚴重擾亂周邊生態系統。

words.tip: 形容詞常帶文學色彩；副詞義“很”較口語化。

ex.zh: 博物館展出了當地民兵曾經穿過的制服。

ex.en: Historical records show that the militia consisted mainly of farmers who trained alongside their regular work.
ex.zh: 歷史記錄顯示，這支民兵主要由農民組成，他們在日常勞作之餘參加訓練。

col: a local militia｜地方民兵組織

words.tip: 指組織；單個成員用a militia member。

ex.en: I poured some cold milk over my cereal.
ex.zh: 我往麥片上倒了些冷牛奶。

ex.en: Milk provides calcium and protein, although people with certain dietary needs may choose suitable alternatives.
ex.zh: 牛奶提供鈣和蛋白質，但有特殊飲食需求的人可以選擇合適的替代品。

ex.zh: 新鮮麵包的香氣與烘焙咖啡的香氣交織在一起。

ex.en: Community festivals allow residents from different backgrounds to mingle, helping build trust and a stronger sense of belonging.
ex.zh: 社區節慶讓不同背景的居民有機會交流，有助於建立信任並增強歸屬感。

words.tip: mingle with既可指與某物混合，也可指與人交往。

ex.zh: 我往檸檬水裡加了新鮮薄荷。

ex.en: Growing herbs such as mint in urban gardens can provide fresh ingredients and encourage interest in food production.
ex.zh: 在城市花園中種植薄荷等香草，可以提供新鮮食材，並激發人們對食物生產的興趣。

words.tip: 植物義通常不可數；a mint可指一顆薄荷糖。

ex.en: The distant pool was only a mirage in the desert.
ex.zh: 遠處的水池只是沙漠中的蜃景。

ex.en: For many young workers, affordable home ownership remains a mirage as property prices rise faster than wages.
ex.zh: 對許多年輕勞動者而言，由於房價漲幅超過工資漲幅，買得起住房仍是可望而不可即的夢想。

words.tip: 指光學蜃景或虛幻希望，不表示普通霧氣。

Very unhappy or uncomfortable

ex.en: I felt miserable when rain ruined our picnic plans.
ex.zh: 大雨毀了我們的野餐計劃，讓我很難過。

ex.en: Overcrowded housing can create miserable living conditions and negatively affect residents' physical and mental health.
ex.zh: 住房過度擁擠會造成惡劣的生活條件，並損害居民的身心健康。

words.tip: 既可形容人的心情，也可形容天氣或生活條件。

ex.zh: 持續不斷的噪聲讓她苦不堪言。

ex.en: Improving access to affordable housing can reduce the misery experienced by families living in overcrowded temporary accommodation.
ex.zh: 改善可負擔住房的供應，可以減輕住在擁擠臨時住所中的家庭所承受的痛苦。

ex.en: Thick curtains helped mitigate the noise from the street.
ex.zh: 厚窗簾幫助減輕了街上傳來的噪聲。

ex.en: Planting trees in urban areas can mitigate the effects of extreme heat and improve residents' quality of life.
ex.zh: 在城市地區植樹可以減輕酷熱的影響，並改善居民的生活質量。

col: mitigate the effects of｜減輕……的影響

words.tip: 正式用詞，直接接風險、損害或影響，不表示徹底消除。

v indicate pain, discomfort, or displeasure

ex.en: He moaned softly as the nurse examined his ankle.
ex.zh: 護士檢查他的腳踝時，他輕輕呻吟著。

ex.en: Rather than moan about unreliable buses, residents could ask local authorities to improve public transport.
ex.zh: 居民與其抱怨公交車不準時，不如向地方政府提出改善公共交通的訴求。

col: let out a moan｜發出一聲呻吟
words.tip: 表示抱怨時較口語化，常用moan about。

ex.zh: 流動圖書館每週五早晨來我們村。

ex.en: Mobile clinics can improve access to basic healthcare for people living in remote rural communities.
ex.zh: 流動診所可以讓偏遠農村社區的居民更容易獲得基本醫療服務。

words.tip: 英式英語常用a mobile指手機；美式常說a cell phone。

ex.zh: 請別嘲笑我的舞姿，我還在學呢。

ex.en: Mock interviews allow students to practise explaining their skills before they apply for their first professional positions.
ex.zh: 模擬面試讓學生在申請第一份專業工作前，練習如何介紹自己的技能。

ex.zh: 晚飯前，我把手機調成了靜音模式。

ex.en: Cycling is an environmentally friendly mode of transport that can also improve public health in urban areas.
ex.zh: 騎行是一種環保的交通方式，也能改善城市居民的健康。

ex.zh: 即使公共交通撥款只小幅增加，也可能改善農村社區的服務。

ex.en: We modified the recipe to use less sugar.
ex.zh: 我們調整了食譜，減少糖的用量。

ex.en: Schools may need to modify their teaching methods to support students with different learning needs.
ex.zh: 學校可能需要調整教學方法，以支持有不同學習需求的學生。

words.tip: 通常指局部調整，不一定是徹底改變。

ex.zh: 他穿著時髦的夾克和擦得鋥亮的靴子來了。

ex.zh: 時髦的室內裝潢起初或許能吸引顧客，但長久的成功取決於可靠的服務和品質。

ex.zh: 公共交通管理部門應為遭到猥褻的乘客提供明確的舉報流程。

def: v be a mystery or bewildering to

tr: a. 無孔的, 無孔隙的
def: a. not porous; especially not having vessels that appear as pores

tr: n. 非放射性
def: a. not radioactive

tr: a. 無意義的, 荒謬的
def: s incongruous; inviting ridicule
s having no intelligible meaning

tr: a. 無法生活的
[醫] 不能生活的
def: s. not capable of living or developing successfully

tr: n. 套索, 束縛, 陷阱
vt. 用套索捉
def: n. a loop formed in a cord or rope by means of a slipknot; it binds tighter as the cord or rope is pulled
v. make a noose in or of
v. secure with a noose

tr: n. 鄉愁, 嚮往過去, 懷舊之情
[醫] 懷鄉病
懷舊；對往昔的眷戀
def: n. longing for something past
warm, sometimes sad feelings about happy times in the past

ex.en: That old song fills me with nostalgia for school.
ex.zh: 那首老歌讓我滿懷對學生時代的眷戀。

ex.en: Nostalgia can encourage communities to preserve historic buildings, even when modern developments promise greater convenience.
ex.zh: 即使現代開發項目有望帶來更多便利，懷舊之情也能促使社區保護歷史建築。

col: nostalgia for the past｜對往昔的眷戀
a wave of nostalgia｜一陣懷舊之情
words.tip: 通常不可數；nostalgia for後接懷念的時期或事物。

tr: n. 萬能藥, 成藥, 妙方
[醫] 秘方
def: n. patent medicine whose efficacy is questionable

tr: n. 著名人士, 值得注意之事物
a. 值得注意的, 顯著的
顯著的；值得注意的
名人；要人
def: n a celebrity who is an inspiration to others
s worthy of notice
s widely known and esteemed

ex.en: Her balcony is notable for its bright yellow flowers.
ex.zh: 她家的陽臺因鮮豔的黃色花朵而引人注目。

ex.en: The city has achieved a notable reduction in air pollution since introducing stricter vehicle standards.
ex.zh: 自實施更嚴格的車輛標準以來，該市的空氣汙染已顯著減少。

col: a notable exception｜值得注意的例外
words.tip: notable for表示因……而出名或引人注意。

tr: vt.以符號表示,把.....寫成記號(或標誌)
def: v. put into notation, as of music or choreography; in the old days, the steps had to be memorized"

tr: n. 刻痕, 等級, 峽谷
vt. 刻凹痕, 用刻痕計算, 贏得
def: n. a V-shaped indentation
n. a V-shaped or U-shaped indentation carved or scratched into a surface
n. a small cut

tr: n. 惡名, 臭名, 聲名狼藉
惡名；聲名狼藉
def: n. the state of being known for some unfavorable act or quality
the state of being widely known for something bad

ex.en: The restaurant gained notoriety for its dirty kitchen.
ex.zh: 這家餐館因廚房髒亂而臭名遠揚。

ex.en: Some companies gain notoriety for environmental damage, making it harder for them to attract skilled workers.
ex.zh: 一些企業因破壞環境而聲名狼藉，因而更難吸引技術人才。

words.tip: 通常不可數，含貶義；中性的“名氣”用fame。

tr: a. 聲名狼藉的, 臭名昭著的, 眾人皆知的
臭名昭著的；聲名狼藉的
def: s known widely and usually unfavorably;
widely known for something bad or undesirable

ex.en: That road is notorious for its deep potholes.
ex.zh: 那條路因坑窪很深而出了名。

ex.en: Cities notorious for severe air pollution often struggle to attract skilled workers and develop sustainable tourism.
ex.zh: 因嚴重空氣汙染而臭名昭著的城市往往難以吸引技術人才和發展可持續旅遊業。

words.tip: 通常含貶義；著名但非負面用famous，不宜用notorious。

tr: adv. 臭名昭著的, 聲名狼藉的
def: r. to a notorious degree

tr: n. 新奇, 新鮮, 新奇的事物
新奇；新穎
新鮮事物
新奇小玩意兒
def: n. originality by virtue of being new and surprising
the quality of being new, unusual, or unfamiliar
something new or unusual that attracts interest

ex.en: The novelty of sleeping in a tent soon wore off.
ex.zh: 睡帳篷的新鮮感很快就消退了。

ex.en: Although the novelty of new technology attracts consumers, long-term adoption depends on practical benefits and affordability.
ex.zh: 雖然新技術的新穎性會吸引消費者，但長期採用仍取決於實際益處和價格是否可負擔。

col: novelty value｜新奇帶來的吸引力
the novelty wears off｜新鮮感消退
words.tip: 指新奇感時不可數；指新鮮事物或小玩意兒時可數。

tr: n. 新手, 初學者
新手；初學者
def: n. someone new to a field or activity
someone with little experience in a particular activity

ex.en: As a gardening novice, I often forget to water seedlings.
ex.zh: 作為園藝新手，我常常忘記給幼苗澆水。

ex.en: Structured mentoring can help a novice develop the confidence needed to manage a classroom effectively.
ex.zh: 有系統的指導能幫助新手建立有效管理課堂所需的信心。

words.tip: 表示某方面的新手，常用a novice at/in。

tr: a. 有害的, 有毒的, 使道德敗壞的
[醫] 有害的, 有毒的
有害的；有毒的
def: a. injurious to physical or mental health
harmful or poisonous to people or other living things

ex.en: Noxious fumes from the spill forced everyone to leave.
ex.zh: 洩漏物產生的有毒煙氣迫使所有人離開。

ex.en: Stricter controls on industrial emissions are needed to protect nearby communities from exposure to noxious gases.
ex.zh: 需要更嚴格地控制工業排放，以保護附近社區免受有毒氣體侵害。

words.tip: 常形容氣體或物質；不只是氣味難聞。

tr: n. 細微差別
細微差別
def: n. a subtle difference in meaning or opinion or attitude
a small difference in meaning, feeling, sound, or appearance

ex.en: Her smile added a playful nuance to the apology.
ex.zh: 她的微笑讓這句道歉多了一絲俏皮意味。

ex.en: Language learners need cultural knowledge to recognise nuances that dictionaries may not fully explain.
ex.zh: 語言學習者需要文化知識，才能辨別詞典可能無法充分解釋的細微差別。

col: nuances of meaning｜意義上的細微差別
capture the nuances｜捕捉細微差別
words.tip: 常用複數nuances，指意義、語氣等細微差別。

tr: a. 適婚的
[醫] 適合結婚的
def: s of girls or women who are eligible to marry

tr: v. (使)成核
a. 有核的
def: v. form into a nucleus

tr: a. 無價值的, 無用的, 無效的, 瑣碎的
def: s. of no real value

tr: a. 無效力的, 無效的, 無價值的
n. 零, 空, 零位
[計] 空
無效的；無法律效力的
零值的；空值的
def: s. lacking any legal or binding force
Having no legal force or effect.
Having a zero value or representing no stored value.

ex.en: The court declared their rental agreement null and void.
ex.zh: 法院宣佈他們的租賃協議無效。

ex.en: A contract may be declared null if one party was forced to accept its terms.
ex.zh: 如果一方被迫接受合同條款，該合同可能被宣佈無效。

words.tip: 法律中常用null and void；編程空值不一定等於零。

tr: vt. 使無效, 廢棄, 取消
[化] 使等於零; 作廢
使失去法律效力
抵消；使無效
def: v declare invalid
v show to be invalid
v make ineffective by counterbalancing the effect of

ex.en: This missing signature could nullify the entire rental agreement.
ex.zh: 缺少這個簽名可能使整份租賃協議失效。

ex.en: Rising energy consumption could nullify the environmental benefits achieved through improvements in industrial efficiency.
ex.zh: 不斷增長的能源消耗可能抵消工業效率提升所帶來的環境效益。

words.tip: 既可指法律上作廢，也可指效果被抵消。

tr: a. 很多的, 數目眾多的, 多數的
[機] 多數的, 甚多的
許多的；眾多的
def: s. amounting to a large indefinite number
Existing in large numbers.

ex.en: Numerous birds gathered around the crumbs on our balcony.
ex.zh: 許多鳥聚在我們陽臺上的麵包屑周圍。

ex.en: Numerous studies suggest that access to green spaces can improve the mental health of urban residents.
ex.zh: 眾多研究表明，能方便地接觸綠地有助於改善城市居民的心理健康。

words.tip: 修飾可數名詞複數，不能直接修飾不可數名詞。

tr: a. 精神上的, 超自然的
def: s. evincing the presence of a deity
a. of or relating to or characteristic of a numen

tr: n. 錢幣(或獎章)收藏家
def: n. a collector and student of money (and coins in particular)

tr: n. 養育, 營養物, 培育
vt. 養育, 供給營養物, 教養
def: n the properties acquired as a consequence of the way you were treated as a child
n helping someone grow up to be an accepted member of the community
v help develop, help grow

tr: a. 營養的, 滋養的
n. 營養物, 滋養物
def: n. any substance (such as a chemical element or inorganic compound) that can be taken in by a green plant and used in organic synthesis

tr: a. 營養的, 滋養的
[醫] 營養的
def: a. of or relating to or providing nutrition

tr: a. 滋養的, 營養的
[醫] 有營養的
def: s of or providing nourishment

tr: n. 綠洲, 舒適的地方
[醫] 綠洲(沙漠中), 健島(病變區中的健康組織)
綠洲
寧靜舒適之地
def: n. a fertile tract in a desert (where the water table approaches the surface)
A place in a desert where water and plants are found.
A peaceful, pleasant place surrounded by something difficult or unpleasant.

ex.en: After hours of walking, we reached a small oasis.
ex.zh: 步行數小時後，我們到達了一片小綠洲。

ex.en: Public gardens provide an oasis of calm for residents living in densely populated urban areas.
ex.zh: 公共花園為生活在人口密集城區的居民提供了一方寧靜之地。

col: an oasis of calm｜寧靜之地
words.tip: 複數為oases；也可比喻喧囂中的寧靜之地。

tr: n. 誓約, 誓言, 咒罵
[法] 誓言, 誓約, 宣誓
誓言；宣誓
def: n. a commitment to tell the truth (especially in a court of law); to lie under oath is to become subject to prosecution for perjury
n. a solemn promise, usually invoking a divine witness, regarding your future acts or behavior
A formal promise to tell the truth or fulfil a duty.

ex.en: The witness took an oath before answering any questions.
ex.zh: 證人在回答任何問題之前先宣了誓。

ex.en: Public officials who swear an oath to serve society should remain accountable for their decisions and conduct.
ex.zh: 宣誓為社會服務的公職人員應對自己的決策和行為負責。

words.tip: under oath指已宣誓說真話，常用於法庭語境。

tr: a. 頑固的, 執拗的, 冷酷的
[法] 執迷不悟的, 毫不悔改的, 無情的
def: s stubbornly persistent in wrongdoing
s showing unfeeling resistance to tender feelings

tr: a. 服從的, 順從的, 孝順的
[法] 服從的, 順從的, 忠順的
def: a. dutifully complying with the commands or instructions of those in authority; the refractory remain unburdened"- Edmund Burke

tr: n. 敬禮, 鞠躬, 敬重
def: n bending the head or body or knee as a sign of reverence or submission or shame or greeting
n the act of obeying; dutiful or submissive behavior with respect to another person

tr: a. 肥胖的
[醫] 肥胖的
肥胖的
def: s excessively fat
having excessive body fat that may harm health

ex.en: The vet said our cat was obese and needed exercise.
ex.zh: 獸醫說我們家的貓過於肥胖，需要運動。

ex.en: People who are obese should have access to supportive healthcare without facing discrimination or blame.
ex.zh: 肥胖人群應能獲得支持性的醫療服務，而不受歧視或責備。

col: clinically obese｜臨床診斷為肥胖的
words.tip: 屬醫學用語，程度通常重於overweight；避免隨意評價他人。

tr: vt. 弄暗, 使模糊, 使迷惑
def: v. make obscure or unclear

tr: n. 異議, 反對, 不喜歡, 缺點, 缺陷, 妨礙, 拒絕之理由
[法] 異議, 反對, 抗議
反對；異議；反對理由
def: n. the speech act of objecting

n. (law) a procedure whereby a party to a suit says that a particular line of questioning or a particular witness or a piece of evidence or other matter is improper and should not be continued and asks the court to rule on its impropriety or illegality
An expression of opposition, or a reason for opposing something.

ex.en: My only objection is that the tickets cost too much.
ex.zh: 我唯一的反對理由是票價太高。

ex.en: Residents raised an objection to the proposed airport expansion because of its likely impact on noise levels.
ex.zh: 居民對擬議的機場擴建提出異議，因為這可能加劇噪聲。

words.tip: objection to中的to是介詞，後接名詞或動名詞。

tr: n. 目的, 目標, 宗旨, 賓格, 實物
a. 客觀的, 如實的, 無偏見的, 賓格的
目標；目的
客觀的；不偏不倚的
def: n. the lens or system of lenses in a telescope or microscope that is nearest the object being viewed
a. undistorted by emotion or personal bias; based on observable phenomena
a. serving as or indicating the object of a verb or of certain prepositions and used for certain other purposes

ex.en: My main objective is to finish the race.
ex.zh: 我的主要目標是跑完全程。

ex.en: Researchers should remain objective when evaluating evidence about the effects of homework on student achievement.
ex.zh: 研究人員在評估家庭作業對學生成績影響的證據時，應保持客觀。

words.tip: 名詞指目標；形容詞指客觀的，反義詞為subjective。

tr: a. 義務的, 必須的, 強制性的
[法] 有拘束的, 強制的, 必須的
def: a. morally or legally constraining or binding
s. required by obligation or compulsion or convention

tr: vt. 強制, 施恩惠於, 使感激
vi. 施恩惠, 幫忙
迫使；使負有義務
幫忙；滿足請求
def: v. bind by an obligation; cause to be indebted
v. provide a service or favor for someone
Require someone to act because of rules or circumstances

ex.en: The sudden storm obliged us to stay indoors.
ex.zh: 突如其來的暴風雨迫使我們待在室內。

ex.en: Environmental regulations oblige manufacturers to reduce harmful emissions and report their progress to public authorities.
ex.zh: 環境法規要求製造商減少有害排放，並向政府部門報告進展。

col: be obliged to do something｜不得不做某事
words.tip: be obliged to do表示被迫或有義務做某事。

tr: a. 樂於施惠的, 體貼的, 有禮貌的
樂於助人的；熱心的
def: v force somebody to do something
v bind by an obligation; cause to be indebted
v provide a service or favor for someone

ex.en: An obliging neighbour watered our plants while we travelled.
ex.zh: 我們旅行時，一位熱心的鄰居幫我們澆了花。

ex.en: Obliging staff can improve patients' experiences by answering questions patiently and responding promptly to reasonable requests.
ex.zh: 樂於助人的工作人員可以通過耐心解答問題、及時回應合理要求來改善患者的體驗。

col: an obliging neighbour｜樂於助人的鄰居
words.tip: obliging 指樂於助人；obliged 常表示被迫或感激。

tr: a. 斜的, 傾斜的, 間接的, 不光明正大的, 躲躲閃閃的
[醫] 斜的
def: n. any grammatical case other than the nominative
a. slanting or inclined in direction or course or position--neither parallel nor perpendicular nor right-angled

tr: vt. 擦去, 沖刷(掉), 消滅, 忘掉, 蓋銷(郵票等)
[法] 滅跡, 消滅, 塗抹
徹底毀滅；抹去
def: v. remove completely from recognition or memory
v. do away with completely, without leaving a trace
Destroy or remove something completely, leaving little or no trace.

ex.en: Heavy snowfall had obliterated every footprint on the garden path.
ex.zh: 大雪已將花園小路上的所有腳印徹底覆蓋。

ex.en: Rapid urban development can obliterate historic neighbourhoods unless effective conservation measures are introduced early in the planning process.
ex.zh: 快速的城市開發可能徹底毀掉歷史街區，除非在規劃初期就引入有效的保護措施。

col: obliterate all traces｜抹去所有痕跡
words.tip: 是動詞，強調徹底消除，比普通 remove 語氣更強。

tr: a. 遺忘的, 健忘的, 不知不覺的
[法] 忘卻的, 健忘的, 不在意的
def: s. (followed by `to' or `of') lacking conscious awareness of

tr: n. 辱罵, 毀謗, 恥辱
def: n. state of disgrace resulting from public abuse

tr: a. 可憎的, 使人不愉快的, 令人討厭的
極討厭的；令人反感的
def: s causing disapproval or protest
extremely unpleasant or offensive

ex.en: An obnoxious passenger played loud music throughout the journey.
ex.zh: 一個討厭的乘客一路都在大聲播放音樂。

ex.en: Obnoxious behaviour on public transport can discourage commuters from using otherwise convenient and affordable services.
ex.zh: 公共交通上的惡劣行為可能讓通勤者不願使用原本便捷又實惠的服務。

words.tip: 語氣比annoying強，常形容無禮的人或行為。

tr: a. 模糊的, 昏暗的, 難解的, 晦澀的, 偏僻的, 微賤的, 無名的
vt. 使變暗, 隱藏, 使變模糊, 使難解
鮮為人知的
費解的；不清楚的
遮蔽；使模糊
def: v. make less visible or unclear
v. make obscure or unclear
v. reduce a vowel to a neutral one, such as a schwa

ex.en: We found an obscure little museum behind the station.
ex.zh: 我們在車站後面發現了一家鮮為人知的小博物館。

ex.en: Overly technical language can obscure important findings, making scientific research less accessible to the public.
ex.zh: 過於專業的語言可能使重要發現變得難以理解，降低公眾瞭解科研成果的便利程度。

col: an obscure writer｜鮮為人知的作家
words.tip: 作形容詞指無名或難懂；作動詞指遮蔽或掩蓋。

tr: n. 陰暗, 朦朧, 晦澀, 費解, 身份低微
def: n. an obscure and unimportant standing; not well known
n. the state of being indistinct or indefinite for lack of adequate illumination

tr: a. 諂媚的, 奉承的, 順從的
def: s. attentive in an ingratiating or servile manner

tr: n. 觀察, 遵守, 儀式, 風俗習慣
[法] 遵守, 奉行, 慣例
遵守；奉行
宗教或傳統儀式
def: n the act of observing; taking a patient look
n a formal event performed on a special occasion
n the act of noticing or paying attention

ex.en: Strict observance of kitchen hygiene keeps our food safe.
ex.zh: 嚴格遵守廚房衛生規範能保障我們的食品安全。

ex.en: Consistent observance of workplace safety regulations can prevent accidents and improve employees' confidence in their employers.
ex.zh: 始終遵守工作場所安全規定能夠預防事故，並增強員工對僱主的信心。

words.tip: observance指遵守或儀式；observation指觀察。

tr: a. 嚴格遵守...的, 留心的, 當心的, 觀察力敏銳的, 注意觀察的
[法] 注意的, 留心的, 嚴格遵守的
def: s. paying close attention especially to details
s. quick to notice; showing quick and keen perception

tr: vt. 迷住, 使困擾
使著迷；使困擾
念念不忘；過分糾結
def: v. be preoccupied with something
to fill someone's mind so they cannot think of anything else
to think about something constantly and excessively

ex.en: Don't obsess over every tiny mark on your shoes.
ex.zh: 別總糾結鞋子上的每一處小汙痕。

ex.en: Some students obsess over examination results, neglecting the broader skills that education should develop.
ex.zh: 一些學生過分關注考試成績，忽視了教育應當培養的更廣泛的能力。

col: obsess over details｜過分糾結細節
be obsessed with success｜痴迷於成功
obsess about appearance｜過分在意外表
words.tip: 常用be obsessed with；主動式常接over或about。

tr: a. 著迷的；無法擺脫的
def: s. influenced or controlled by a powerful force such as a strong emotion

tr: n. 困擾, 困擾人的情緒
[醫] 強迫觀念
def: n. an unhealthy and compulsive preoccupation with something or someone

tr: a. 著迷的
過度痴迷的；執念的
def: n. a person who has obsessions
Thinking about something constantly and finding it difficult to stop.

ex.en: His obsessive checking of the weather delayed our picnic.
ex.zh: 他沒完沒了地查看天氣，耽誤了我們的野餐。

ex.en: Obsessive concern about academic performance can prevent students from maintaining healthy friendships and enjoying leisure activities.
ex.zh: 過度關注學業表現可能會妨礙學生維持健康的友誼和享受休閒活動。

col: obsessive about details｜過度糾結細節
words.tip: 比interested強得多，常含過度、難以自控之意。

tr: a. 在逐步廢棄的

n. an obstruction that stands in the way (and must be removed or surmounted or circumvented)

阻撓；妨礙

n. the physical condition of blocking or filling a passage with an obstruction
n. the act of obstructing

ex.en: A fallen branch caused an obstruction on the narrow path.
ex.zh: 一根掉落的樹枝擋住了狹窄的小路。

ex.en: Removing unnecessary administrative procedures can reduce obstruction to the development of small businesses in rural areas.
ex.zh: 取消不必要的行政程序可以減少農村地區小企業發展面臨的阻礙。

words.tip: 實體障礙物通常可數；阻撓這一行為常不可數。

tr: a. 能得到的
可獲得的
def: s capable of being obtained
possible to get or acquire

ex.en: Replacement parts are easily obtainable from the local shop.
ex.zh: 替換零件在當地商店很容易買到。

ex.en: Reliable information about public health services should be readily obtainable by all members of society.
ex.zh: 社會所有成員都應能方便地獲取有關公共衛生服務的可靠信息。

col: widely obtainable｜很多地方都能獲得的
words.tip: obtainable強調能獲取；來源常用from引出。

tr: vt. 逼使, 強迫, 伸出
vi. 打擾, 強行闖入
def: v push to thrust outward
v thrust oneself in as if by force

tr: a. 鈍的, 不鋒利的, 愚鈍的
[醫] 鈍形的, 遲鈍的(智力)
def: a. of an angle; between 90 and 180 degrees
s. (of a leaf shape) rounded at the apex
s. lacking in insight or discernment

tr: n. (錢幣、獎章等)正面, 主要的一面, 對立面
a. 正面的, 對應面的, 倒轉的
def: n. the more conspicuous of two alternatives or cases or sides
n. the side of a coin or medal bearing the principal stamp or design

tr: vt. 除去, 排除, 使成為不必要, 避免

明顯的；顯而易見的
def: a. easily perceived by the senses or grasped by the mind
Easy to notice or understand.

ex.en: The muddy footprints made the dog's hiding place obvious.
ex.zh: 泥腳印讓狗的藏身處一目瞭然。

ex.en: The environmental benefits of cycling are obvious, but safer routes are needed to encourage more people to cycle.
ex.zh: 騎自行車的環境效益顯而易見，但還需更安全的路線來鼓勵更多人騎行。

col: for obvious reasons｜出於顯而易見的原因
obvious to everyone｜人人都看得出來
words.tip: 常用It is obvious that…表示“顯然……”。

tr: a. 偶然的, 臨時的
[法] 偶然的, 特殊場合的
偶爾的；不經常的
def: s. occurring from time to time
happening sometimes, but not often or regularly

ex.en: We enjoy an occasional picnic beside the river.
ex.zh: 我們喜歡偶爾到河邊野餐。

ex.en: Even occasional access to green spaces can improve the wellbeing of people living in crowded cities.
ex.zh: 即使只是偶爾接觸綠地，也能改善擁擠城市居民的身心健康。

col: an occasional user｜偶爾使用的人
words.tip: occasional修飾名詞；occasionally修飾動詞。

tr: vt. 使閉塞, 隔斷, 擋住
vi. 咬合
def: v block passage through

v. 掩蔽, 隱藏
n. 神秘之事, 神秘學
def: n. supernatural practices and techniques
v. become concealed or hidden from view or have its light extinguished
v. hide from view

tr: n. 職業, 佔有, 佔有期, 佔領, 佔領軍
[經] 佔有, 佔用, 職業
職業；工作
軍事佔領
居住；使用
def: n. the principal activity in your life that you do to earn money
n. the control of a country by military forces of a foreign power
n. any activity that occupies a person's attention

ex.en: Her occupation involves repairing bicycles in a small workshop.
ex.zh: 她的工作是在一家小修理鋪裡修自行車。

ex.en: A person's occupation can influence their income, social connections, and opportunities for further education.
ex.zh: 一個人的職業會影響其收入、社會關係以及繼續深造的機會。

words.tip: 表示職業時較正式，常見於表格；不要與職位混同。

tr: a. 眼睛的, 用眼的, 憑視覺的, 目擊的
n. 目鏡
def: a. of or relating to or resembling the eye
a. relating to or using sight
s. visible; give me the ocular proof"- Shakespeare

tr: n. 頌詩, 賦
def: n. a lyric poem with complex stanza forms

tr: a. 可憎的, 可厭的, 醜惡的

tr: n. 憎惡, 討厭, 臭名
def: n. state of disgrace resulting from detestable behavior

tr: n. 里程錶
車輛里程錶
def: n. a meter that shows mileage traversed
a device measuring the total distance a vehicle has travelled

ex.en: The odometer showed how far we had driven.
ex.zh: 里程錶顯示了我們已經行駛的距離。

ex.en: When purchasing a used vehicle, consumers should check its odometer reading alongside its maintenance records.
ex.zh: 購買二手車時，消費者應將里程錶讀數與保養記錄一併核查。

words.tip: 記錄累計里程；speedometer顯示即時車速。

tr: a. 散發氣味的, 臭的
def: s. morally offensive
s. emitting an odor
s. having a natural fragrance

tr: a. 無嗅的, 沒有氣味的
def: a. having no odor

tr: a. 走調的, 不正常的, 不適合的, 不和諧的
def: s inaccurate in pitch

tr: a. 不平常的, 離奇的, 不落俗套的
n. 弱拍
def: n an unaccented beat (especially the last beat of a measure)
s informal terms; strikingly unconventional

tr: v. 犯罪, 冒犯, 違反, 進攻
def: v cause to feel resentment or indignation
v act in disregard of laws, rules, contracts, or promises
v strike with disgust or revulsion

tr: a. 令人不快的, 侮辱的, 攻擊性的
[法] 攻擊的, 進攻的, 冒犯的
冒犯的；令人反感的
進攻性的
攻勢；集中行動
def: s. violating or tending to violate or offend against
a. for the purpose of attack rather than defense
a. causing anger or annoyance

ex.en: He apologised when he realised his joke was offensive.
ex.zh: 他意識到自己的玩笑冒犯了別人，便道了歉。

ex.en: Schools should address offensive behaviour promptly while helping students understand why their words can hurt others.
ex.zh: 學校應及時處理冒犯行為，同時幫助學生理解為什麼自己的言語會傷害他人。

col: find something offensive｜覺得某事令人反感
words.tip: 表示覺得被冒犯用offended，不用offensive。

tr: a. 即時的, 即席的, 無準備的, 隨便的, 簡慢的, 不友好的
adv. 即時地, 即席地, 隨便地
未經查證地；不假思索地
漫不經心的；簡慢的
def: s. casually thoughtless or inconsiderate
r. without previous thought or preparation
r. in a casually inconsiderate manner

ex.en: I can't remember the address offhand, but I'll check.
ex.zh: 我一時記不起地址，不過我會查一下。

ex.en: An offhand response to a patient's concerns may undermine trust, even when the medical advice is accurate.
ex.zh: 對患者的擔憂回應得漫不經心，即使醫療建議準確，也可能損害信任。

words.tip: 副詞常與否定句連用，表示不查資料就答不上來。

tr: a. 多管閒事的, 非官方的
[法] 非官方的, 非正式的
def: s intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner

tr: a. 不親熱的, 冷漠的, 疏遠的, 健康較差的
def: s. lacking cordiality; unfriendly

tr: n. 抵消, 把...並列, 旁系, 支管, 用膠印法印
vt. 彌補, 抵消, 膠印
vi. 裝支管
n. 偏移量
[計] 偏移量
def: n. a plate makes an inked impression on a rubber-blanketed cylinder, which in turn transfers it to the paper
v. compensate for or counterbalance
v. cause (printed matter) to transfer or smear onto another surface

ex.en: My shorter commute offsets the higher rent here.
ex.zh: 通勤時間縮短彌補了這裡租金較高的不足。

ex.en: Planting trees can offset some carbon emissions, but reducing fossil fuel consumption remains essential.
ex.zh: 植樹可以抵消一部分碳排放，但減少化石燃料消耗仍然至關重要。

words.tip: 過去式和過去分詞仍為offset；現在分詞為offsetting。

tr: n. 子孫, 後代, 產物
[法] 後輩, 子孫, 後裔
子女；後代；幼崽
def: n. the immediate descendants of a person
n. something that comes into existence as a result
The children or young of a person, animal, or plant.

ex.en: The mother duck led her offspring safely across the path.
ex.zh: 鴨媽媽帶著小鴨們安全地穿過小路。

ex.en: Many species invest considerable energy in protecting their offspring, which increases the young animals' chances of survival.
ex.zh: 許多物種投入大量精力保護後代，從而提高幼崽的存活機會。

col: protect their offspring｜保護它們的幼崽
words.tip: 單複數同形；談人的子女時比children正式。

tr: n. 臺後, 幕內
a. 臺後的, 幕內的
def: a. situated or taking place in the area of a stage not visible to the audience
s. concealed from public view or attention
r. behind the scenes; not on stage

tr: n. 眉目傳情
vt. 挑逗地注視
vi. 做媚眼
def: v. look at with amorous intentions

[化] 軟膏; 藥膏
def: n. semisolid preparation (usually containing a medicine) applied externally as a remedy or for soothing an irritation

[醫] 油脂性的, 油狀的
def: s unpleasantly and excessively suave or ingratiating in manner or speech
s containing an unusual amount of grease or oil

tr: a. 嗅覺的, 味道的
n. 嗅覺器官, 嗅神經
def: a. of or relating to olfaction

tr: n. 煎蛋卷, 煎蛋餅, 炒蛋
def: n. beaten eggs or an egg mixture cooked until just set; may be folded around e.g. ham or cheese or jelly

tr: a. 惡兆的, 不吉利的, 預兆的
不祥的；預示危險的
def: s threatening or foreshadowing evil or tragic developments
s presaging ill fortune
suggesting that something bad or unpleasant may happen

ex.en: Ominous clouds gathered as we hurried back home.
ex.zh: 陰沉得令人不安的烏雲聚攏過來，我們趕忙往家走。

ex.en: The rapid decline in insect populations is an ominous sign for ecosystems that depend on pollination.
ex.zh: 對於依賴授粉的生態系統而言，昆蟲數量迅速下降是一個不祥的徵兆。

col: an ominous silence｜令人不安的寂靜
words.tip: 強調預示壞事將發生，而非壞事已經發生。

tr: vt. 省略, 刪除, 疏忽, 遺漏
[化] 省略
省略；遺漏
def: v prevent from being included or considered or accepted
v leave undone or leave out
to leave something out, deliberately or accidentally

ex.en: You can omit the chilli if you prefer milder soup.
ex.zh: 如果喜歡清淡些的湯，可以不放辣椒。

ex.en: Reports that omit important evidence may give policymakers an inaccurate picture of the challenges facing local communities.
ex.zh: 遺漏重要證據的報告，可能使政策制定者誤判當地社區面臨的挑戰。

col: omit something from a report｜從報告中刪去某項內容
words.tip: 過去式omitted，進行式omitting，均雙寫t。

tr: a. 全能的, 無所不能的, 徹頭徹尾的, 臭名昭著的
def: s having unlimited power

tr: a. 無所不在的, 普通存在的
def: s. being present everywhere at once

tr: a. 全知的, 無所不知的
n. 無所不知者, 上帝
def: s infinitely wise

tr: a. 無所不吃的, 雜食的, 什麼都喜歡的
def: a. feeding on both plants and animals

tr: a. 繁重的, 負有法律責任的
[法] 負有義務的, 艱鉅的, 繁重的
def: s not easily borne; wearing; I only had to greet the guests"

tr: a. 前進的, 進行的, 不間斷的
n. 前進, 發展
正在進行的；持續的
def: s. currently happening
Continuing to happen or develop, rather than being finished.

ex.en: The ongoing repairs mean we cannot use the kitchen.
ex.zh: 維修仍在進行，所以我們沒法使用廚房。

ex.en: Ongoing research into renewable energy is essential for reducing dependence on fossil fuels and limiting environmental damage.
ex.zh: 持續開展可再生能源研究，對減少化石燃料依賴和限制環境損害至關重要。

col: an ongoing investigation｜正在進行的調查
words.tip: 強調尚在持續，不等於即將發生的upcoming。

tr: n. 開始, 攻擊, 進攻
[醫] 起始, 開始
開始；發作
def: n. the beginning or early stages
The beginning of something, especially something unpleasant.

ex.en: The sudden onset of rain sent us running indoors.
ex.zh: 突然下起雨來，我們趕緊跑進屋裡。

ex.en: Regular physical activity may delay the onset of certain chronic diseases and improve overall wellbeing.
ex.zh: 經常進行體育活動可能延緩某些慢性病的發生，並改善整體健康狀況。

col: the onset of symptoms｜症狀的出現
the onset of winter｜冬季的來臨
words.tip: 常用the onset of，多指疾病或不利情況的開始。

tr: n. 突擊, 猛擊, 猛攻
def: n. a sudden and severe onset of trouble

tr: n. 負擔, 責任, 義務, 過失, 恥辱
[法] 責任, 義務, 負擔
def: n an onerous or difficult concern

tr: n. 滲流, 分泌物
v. 滲出, 洩漏
def: n any thick, viscous matter
n the process of seeping
v pass gradually or leak through or as if through small openings

tr: n. 不透明, 電波不透過, 不透明體
[醫] 渾濁, 不透明, 不透光, 不透明區, 濁斑
def: n. the phenomenon of not permitting the passage of electromagnetic radiation
n. incomprehensibility resulting from obscurity of meaning
n. the quality of being opaque to a degree; the degree to which something reduces the passage of light

tr: n. 乳白光, 蛋白色光
[化] 乳光
def: n. the visual property of something having a milky brightness and a play of colors from the surface

[醫] 乳光的, 乳色的
def: s having a play of lustrous rainbow colors

tr: n. 不透明物
a. 不透明的, 不傳熱的, 不傳導的, 陰暗的
[計] 白底
def: a. not transmitting or reflecting light or radiant energy; impenetrable to sight
s. not clearly understood or expressed

tr: a. 可操作的, 可實施的, 可手術治療的
[醫] 可行手術的
def: a. capable of being treated by surgical operation
s. usable for a specific purpose

tr: a. 動作的, 運轉的, 有效的, 關鍵的, 手術的
n. 技工, 偵探
def: a. being in force or having or exerting force
s. effective; producing a desired effect

tr: v. 想, 以為
def: v. express one's opinion openly and without fear or hesitation

tr: a. 固執己見的, 武斷的
def: s. obstinate in your opinions

tr: n. 對手, 敵手, 反對者
a. 敵對的, 反對的, 對面的
def: s. characterized by active hostility

tr: a. 恰好的, 時機適宜的, 適當的
def: a. suitable or at a time that is suitable or advantageous especially for a particular purpose

tr: vt. 反對, 以...對抗, 抗爭
vi. 反對
反對；抵制
def: v. be against; express opposition to
v. contrast with equal weight or force
v. be resistant to

ex.en: Our neighbours oppose building a road through the park.
ex.zh: 我們的鄰居反對修建一條穿過公園的道路。

ex.en: Many residents oppose airport expansion because they fear increased noise and damage to local wildlife habitats.
ex.zh: 許多居民反對機場擴建，因為他們擔心噪聲增加以及當地野生動物棲息地受損。

col: oppose a proposal｜反對一項提議
words.tip: oppose 後直接接名詞或動名詞，不加 to。

tr: a. 反對的, 敵對的, 對抗的, 相對的
[機] 反對的, 相反的, 對立的
def: a. being in opposition or having an opponent

tr: a. 相對的, 相反的, 對面的
prep. 對面
n. 對立面
相反的；對面的
在…對面
def: s. being directly across from each other; facing
a. of leaves etc; growing in pairs on either side of a stem
s. moving or facing away from each other

ex.en: We left the station and walked in opposite directions.
ex.zh: 我們離開車站，朝相反的方向走去。

ex.en: Although the policy aimed to reduce traffic, it had the opposite effect in several residential areas.
ex.zh: 儘管該政策旨在減少交通流量，卻在幾個住宅區產生了相反的效果。

col: the exact opposite｜截然相反的事物
words.tip: 介詞opposite後直接接地點；名詞常用the opposite of。

tr: vt. 壓迫, 壓抑, 使煩惱
def: v. come down on or keep down by unjust use of one's authority

tr: a. 壓制性的, 壓迫的, 沉重的
def: s. weighing heavily on the senses or spirit
s. marked by unjust severity or arbitrary behavior

tr: a. 嘴不乾淨的, 無禮的, 粗野的, 辱罵的, 該罵的
def: s expressing offensive reproach
s (used of conduct or character) deserving or bringing disgrace or shame

tr: a. 眼睛的, 視覺的, 光學的
[機] 光學上的, 光學的
光的；光學的
視覺的；視力的
def: a. of or relating to or involving light or optics
Relating to light or devices that use light.
Relating to sight or the way the eyes work.

ex.en: This optical illusion makes the flat drawing look three-dimensional.
ex.zh: 這種視錯覺讓平面的圖畫看起來像立體的。

ex.en: Optical fibres enable rapid data transmission, supporting the expansion of reliable internet access in remote communities.
ex.zh: 光纖能實現快速數據傳輸，幫助可靠的互聯網服務覆蓋偏遠社區。

words.tip: optical涉及光或視覺；optical illusion指視錯覺。

tr: a. 最佳的, 最理想的
[化] 最優的
最佳的；最適宜的
def: s most desirable possible under a restriction expressed or implied
Best or most effective for a particular purpose.

ex.en: This sunny windowsill provides optimal conditions for my herbs.
ex.zh: 這個陽光充足的窗臺為我的香草提供了最適宜的生長條件。

ex.en: Urban planners must balance housing density and green space to achieve optimal living conditions for residents.
ex.zh: 城市規劃者必須平衡住房密度與綠地面積，為居民創造最佳居住條件。

words.tip: 已含“最佳”之意，通常不再用 most 修飾。

[醫] 樂觀主義, 樂觀
樂觀；樂觀態度

n. a general disposition to expect the best in all things

ex.en: Her optimism helped us stay cheerful during the storm.
ex.zh: 暴風雨期間，她的樂觀讓我們保持了好心情。

ex.en: Despite economic uncertainty, many graduates express optimism about their chances of finding meaningful employment.
ex.zh: 儘管經濟形勢不明朗，許多畢業生仍對找到有意義的工作持樂觀態度。

col: optimism about the future｜對未來的樂觀態度
words.tip: 不可數名詞；對某事樂觀常用optimism about。

tr: n. 樂觀者, 樂觀主義者
def: n. a person disposed to take a favorable view of things

tr: a. 樂觀的, 樂觀主義的, 樂天的
樂觀的；抱有希望的
def: a. expecting the best in this best of all possible worlds
Expecting good things to happen or a situation to improve.

ex.en: Despite the rain, we remained optimistic about our picnic.
ex.zh: 雖然下著雨，我們仍對野餐抱有希望。

ex.en: Many graduates remain optimistic about their career prospects despite increasing competition in the labour market.
ex.zh: 儘管勞動力市場的競爭日益激烈，許多畢業生仍對自己的職業前景保持樂觀。

words.tip: 常用be optimistic about；反義詞是pessimistic。

tr: n. 最適條件, 最佳效果
a. 最優的, 最適宜的
最適宜的；最佳的
最佳狀態；最適量
def: n. most favorable conditions or greatest degree or amount possible under given circumstances
s. most desirable possible under a restriction expressed or implied
best suited to achieving a particular result

ex.en: This sunny windowsill provides optimum conditions for my herbs.
ex.zh: 這個陽光充足的窗臺為我種的香草提供了最適宜的條件。

ex.en: Maintaining the optimum classroom temperature can help students concentrate and reduce the energy required for heating.
ex.zh: 保持最適宜的教室溫度有助於學生集中注意力，並減少供暖能耗。

words.tip: 強調最適合目標，並非越多越好；通常不用most修飾。

tr: n. 富裕, 豐富, 大量
def: n wealth as evidenced by sumptuous living

tr: a. 富裕的, 豪華的, 奢侈的, 豐富的, 大量的
def: s rich and superior in quality

tr: n. 神諭, 神諭處, 預言
def: n. a prophecy (usually obscure or allegorical) revealed by a priest or priestess; believed to be infallible
n. a shrine where an oracular god is consulted

tr: a. 神諭的, 神諭似的, 謎似的, 玄妙深奧的
def: a. of or relating to an oracle

tr: n. 演講, 雄辯術, 演講術, 雄辯
def: n. addressing an audience formally (usually a long and rhetorical address and often pompous)

tr: a. 軌道的, 眼眶的
[化] 軌道
def: a. of or relating to an orbit
a. of or relating to the eye socket

tr: n. 果園, 果樹林
def: n garden consisting of a small cultivated wood without undergrowth

tr: v. 編管絃樂曲
def: v. write an orchestra score for

tr: vt. 註定, 規定, 任命
vi. 頒佈命令
def: v. order by virtue of superior authority; decree
v. appoint to a clerical posts
v. invest with ministerial or priestly authority

tr: n. 嚴酷考驗, 痛苦經歷, 煎熬
[法] 神裁判法, 嚴酷的考驗, 痛苦的經驗
痛苦的經歷；嚴峻考驗
def: n. a severe or trying experience

n. a primitive method of determining a person's guilt or innocence by subjecting the accused person to dangerous or painful tests believed to be under divine control; escape was usually taken as a sign of innocence
A difficult or frightening experience that lasts for some time.

ex.en: Getting home through the storm was a real ordeal.
ex.zh: 穿過暴風雨回家真是一次痛苦的經歷。

ex.en: For displaced families, finding secure housing can become a prolonged ordeal without adequate public support.
ex.zh: 對於流離失所的家庭，若缺乏充分的公共支持，尋找安全住房可能成為漫長的煎熬。

col: go through an ordeal｜經歷磨難
a traumatic ordeal｜造成心理創傷的經歷
words.tip: 指令人痛苦或恐懼的經歷，不用於普通的小麻煩。

tr: n. 法令, 條例, 聖餐禮
[經] 法令, 條款, 條例
def: n. a statute enacted by a city government

tr: a. 平常的, 普通的, 平凡的
n. 平常的人(或事)
普通的；平常的
def: n. a judge of a probate court
n. the expected or commonplace condition or situation
n. a clergyman appointed to prepare condemned prisoners for death

ex.en: It looked like an ordinary box until we opened it.
ex.zh: 打開之前，它看起來就是一個普通盒子。

ex.en: Urban planning should reflect the needs of ordinary residents rather than focus exclusively on attracting wealthy investors.
ex.zh: 城市規劃應反映普通居民的需求，而不是隻顧吸引富有的投資者。

words.tip: ordinary強調不特別；不等於表示平均水平的average。

tr: n. 生物, 有機體, 社會組織
[醫] 生物[體],[有]機體
def: n. a living thing that has (or can develop) the ability to act or function independently
n. a system considered analogous in structure or function to a living body

tr: n. 東方, 東方諸國
a. 東方的
vi. 向東
vt. 使朝東, 使適應, 確定方向
def: v. be oriented
v. determine one's position with reference to another point
v. cause to point

tr: a. 最初的, 原始的, 有創意的
n. 原物, 原作
最初的；原來的
獨創的；新穎的
原件；原作
def: n. something that serves as a model or a basis for making copies
s. preceding all others in time or being as first made or performed
s. (of e.g. information) not secondhand or by way of something intermediary

ex.en: The kitchen still has its original wooden floor.
ex.zh: 廚房仍保留著原來的木地板。

ex.en: Schools should encourage original thinking rather than reward students only for repeating information from textbooks.
ex.zh: 學校應鼓勵獨創性思考，而不是隻獎勵複述課本知識的學生。

words.tip: 可指最初的，也可指原創的；看語境區分。

tr: n. 裝飾物, 觀賞植物
a. 裝飾性的, 裝飾的, 觀賞用的
def: n. any plant grown for its beauty or ornamental value

tr: a. 裝飾的, 華麗的
def: s marked by elaborate rhetoric and elaborated with decorative details

tr: a. 下等的, 低劣的, 脾氣壞的, 故意刁難的
def: s having a difficult and contrary disposition

tr: a. 朗朗的, 誇大的, 做作的
def: s. (of sounds) full and rich

tr: a. 正統的, 傳統的, 慣常的
東正教的
猶太教正統派的
def: a. of or pertaining to or characteristic of Judaism
a. adhering to what is commonly accepted
a. of or relating to or characteristic of the Eastern Orthodox Church

ex.en: We visited an Orthodox church with beautiful painted icons.
ex.zh: 我們參觀了一座裝飾著精美聖像畫的東正教教堂。

ex.en: Preserving Orthodox churches can protect architectural heritage while helping visitors understand the religious traditions of local communities.
ex.zh: 保護東正教教堂既能保存建築遺產，也能幫助遊客瞭解當地社區的宗教傳統。

words.tip: 大寫常指宗教派別；小寫orthodox可指正統的、傳統的。

tr: vi. 振動, 彷徨, 猶豫
vt. 使振動, 使動搖
擺動；振盪
搖擺不定；波動
def: v. move or swing from side to side regularly
To move repeatedly backwards and forwards.
To keep changing between different feelings, opinions, or levels.

ex.en: The fan oscillates slowly, cooling both sides of the room.
ex.zh: 風扇緩緩來回轉動，給房間兩側都送去涼風。

ex.en: Public opinion can oscillate between support and opposition as new information about environmental policies emerges.
ex.zh: 隨著有關環境政策的新信息出現，公眾意見可能在支持與反對之間搖擺。

col: oscillate between extremes｜在極端之間搖擺
words.tip: 表示在兩者間搖擺，用oscillate between A and B。

tr: n. 滲透作用, 滲透性, 潛移默化, 耳濡目染
[化] 滲透; 滲透作用
def: n. (biology, chemistry) diffusion of molecules through a semipermeable membrane from a place of higher concentration to a place of lower concentration until the concentration on both sides is equal

tr: a. 骨的, 骨質的, 多骨的
[醫] 骨的, 骨性的
def: a. composed of or containing bone

tr: vt. 使骨化, 使硬化, 使僵化
vi. 骨化, 硬化, 變得極端保守
def: v. become bony
v. cause to become hard and bony

tr: a. 表面的, 假裝的, 看得出的
[經] 表面的, 詭稱的
表面上的；聲稱的
def: s. represented or appearing as such; pretended
Stated or appearing to be true, but possibly not genuine

ex.en: His ostensible reason for visiting was to return my umbrella.
ex.zh: 他來訪的表面理由是歸還我的雨傘。

ex.en: The ostensible purpose of the policy was environmental protection, although it also benefited domestic manufacturers.
ex.zh: 這項政策聲稱旨在保護環境，但它也使國內製造商受益。

words.tip: 暗示表象可能不是真相，但不等於已證實虛假。

tr: n. 虛飾, 虛有其表, 賣弄
炫耀；擺闊
def: n. a gaudy outward display
n. lack of elegance as a consequence of being pompous and puffed up with vanity
n. pretentious or showy or vulgar display

ex.en: Their wedding was warm and cheerful, without any ostentation.
ex.zh: 他們的婚禮溫馨愉快，沒有絲毫鋪張炫耀。

ex.en: The ostentation associated with luxury consumption can intensify social pressure to display wealth rather than save responsibly.
ex.zh: 奢侈消費中的炫富行為可能加劇社會壓力，促使人們展示財富而非理性儲蓄。

col: an air of ostentation｜炫耀的氣派
words.tip: 不可數名詞，通常含貶義，強調故意展示以引人注目。

tr: a. 裝飾表面的, 鋪張的, 誇示的, 華美的, 顯眼的
def: a. intended to attract notice and impress others
s. (of a display) tawdry or vulgar

tr: n. 流放, 放逐, 排斥
[法] 流放, 放逐, 排斥
def: n. the act of excluding someone from society by general consent

tr: vt. 流放, 放逐, 排斥
def: v. avoid speaking to or dealing with

tr: a. 不必要的, 怠惰的, 沒有用的, 多餘的
def: s. serving no useful purpose; having no excuse for being

tr: vt. 逐出, 罷黜, 剝奪, 驅逐
[法] 驅逐, 剝奪, 免職
罷黜；趕下臺；驅逐
def: v. remove from a position or office
v. remove and replace
To force someone out of a position or place.

ex.en: Club members voted to oust their unpopular chair.
ex.zh: 俱樂部成員投票罷免了不受歡迎的主席。

ex.en: Shareholders may seek to oust company directors who repeatedly fail to meet environmental commitments or financial targets.
ex.zh: 股東可能尋求罷免那些屢次未能履行環保承諾或實現財務目標的公司董事。

col: oust someone from office｜將某人趕下臺
be ousted as chair｜被罷免主席職務
words.tip: 常用oust someone from office，強調被迫離職。

tr: n. 爆發, 突發, 破裂, 暴亂
def: n. a sudden intense happening
n. a sudden violent disturbance

tr: a. 舊式的, 落伍的, 過時的
過時的；陳舊的
def: s. old; no longer valid or fashionable
No longer useful or suitable because things have changed.

ex.en: This outdated map doesn't show the new train station.
ex.zh: 這張過時的地圖沒有標出新火車站。

ex.en: Hospitals need adequate funding to replace outdated equipment and provide safer, more effective treatment for patients.
ex.zh: 醫院需要充足的資金來更換陳舊設備，為患者提供更安全、更有效的治療。

words.tip: 強調因時代變化而不再適用，不只是年代久遠。

tr: vt. 以計取勝
def: v. outdo someone in trickery

tr: n. 外出, 開支, 流出
a. 喜歡外出的, 即將離職的, 樂於助人的
def: a. leaving a place or a position
a. retiring from a position or office

tr: vt. 過大而不適於, 長得比...高(或大、快), 成長得不再具有...
def: v. grow too large or too mature for
v. grow faster than

tr: n. 自然的發展, 結果, 副產物, 分枝
[醫] 贅疣
def: n. a natural consequence of development

tr: a. 外國氣派的, 偏僻的, 古怪的
稀奇古怪的；荒誕的
def: s conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
extremely unusual or strange, often seeming unreasonable

ex.en: He arrived wearing an outlandish hat shaped like a pineapple.
ex.zh: 他戴著一頂形似菠蘿的古怪帽子來了。

ex.en: Although some environmental proposals initially seem outlandish, they may eventually inspire practical solutions to urban pollution.
ex.zh: 雖然一些環保提議起初看似荒誕，卻可能最終為解決城市汙染提供切實可行的思路。

words.tip: 強調異乎尋常，常帶驚訝或不贊同的語氣。

tr: vt. 比...長久, 從...中逃生
def: v live longer than

tr: n. 出口, 發洩方法, 市場
[醫] 出口
銷售網點；專賣店
表達渠道；宣洩途徑
出口；排放口
def: n a place of business for retailing goods
n receptacle providing a place in a wiring system where current can be taken to run electrical devices
n an opening that permits escape or release

ex.en: A new clothing outlet opened near the station yesterday.
ex.zh: 昨天車站附近新開了一家服裝店。

ex.en: Community arts programmes provide a valuable outlet for young people to express emotions and develop confidence.
ex.zh: 社區藝術項目為年輕人表達情感、培養自信提供了寶貴的渠道。

col: creative outlet｜發揮創造力的途徑
an outlet for frustration｜宣洩挫敗感的途徑
words.tip: outlet for常指表達渠道；美式英語中也指電源插座。

tr: n. 大綱, 輪廓, 概要
vt. 描畫輪廓, 描述要點
n. 大綱, 分級, 輪廓
[計] 大綱, 分級, 輪廓
概要；大綱
def: n. the line that appears to bound an object
n. a sketchy summary of the main points of an argument or theory
n. a schematic or preliminary plan

ex.en: I wrote a quick outline before starting my essay.
ex.zh: 開始寫作文之前，我先快速列了一個提綱。

ex.en: The report outlines several practical measures that schools can adopt to support students with learning difficulties.
ex.zh: 這份報告概述了學校可以採取的幾項切實措施，以幫助有學習困難的學生。

words.tip: 表示概要時強調主要內容，不包含詳細論述。

tr: a. 在外的, 邊遠的, 偏僻的, 題外的
def: s. relatively far from a center or middle

tr: vt. 對(敵手)機動制勝, 智勝, 在謀略上勝過(敵人)
def: v. defeat by more skillful maneuvering

tr: a. 過時的, 廢棄的
[經] (式樣等)過時的, 廢棄了的
def: v make unfashionable, outdated, or obsolete
s out of fashion

tr: n. 著手, 開頭, 最初
開始；開端
def: n the time at which something is supposed to begin
The beginning of an activity, process, or period.

ex.en: We agreed on a budget at the outset.
ex.zh: 我們一開始就商定了預算。

ex.en: Community members should be involved from the outset when local authorities plan major housing developments.
ex.zh: 地方政府規劃大型住宅開發項目時，就應從一開始讓社區成員參與。

words.tip: 常用於at/from the outset，不用於set outset。

tr: vt. 光亮強過..., 使相形見絀, 使失色
vi. 發光
def: v. shine brighter than
v. attract more attention and praise than others

tr: a. 直言無諱的, 坦率的, 坦白無隱的
def: s. given to expressing yourself freely or insistently

tr: vt. 追過, 勝過, 凌駕
def: v be or do something to a greater degree
v go far ahead of

tr: vt. 比...重, 比...重要, 比...有價值
def: v. be heavier than

tr: vt. 瞞騙, 以智取勝
def: v. beat through cleverness and wit

tr: n. 橢圓形
a. 卵形的, 橢圓形的
橢圓形的；卵形的
橢圓形；卵形
def: n a closed plane curve resulting from the intersection of a circular cone and a plane cutting completely through it
s rounded like an egg
Having a rounded shape that is longer than it is wide.

ex.en: She served the roast vegetables on an oval plate.
ex.zh: 她用一個橢圓形盤子盛烤蔬菜。

ex.en: The proposed park includes an oval pond surrounded by native plants to provide habitats for local wildlife.
ex.zh: 規劃中的公園設有一個橢圓形池塘，周圍種植本地植物，為當地野生動物提供棲息地。

words.tip: oval可作形容詞或名詞；an oval指一個橢圓形。

tr: n. 烤箱, 灶, 子宮
[化] 烘箱
烤箱；烤爐
def: n. kitchen appliance used for baking or roasting
an enclosed appliance used to bake or roast food

ex.en: The bread is still warm from the oven.
ex.zh: 麵包剛出烤箱，還熱乎著。

ex.en: Using an energy-efficient oven can reduce household electricity consumption without changing cooking habits significantly.
ex.zh: 使用節能烤箱可以減少家庭用電量，而不必大幅改變烹飪習慣。

col: bake in the oven｜放入烤箱烘烤
words.tip: oven指封閉烤箱；爐頂灶具通常叫hob或stove。

tr: vt. 威懾, 嚇服
def: v. subdue, restrain, or overcome by affecting with a feeling of awe; frighten (as with threats)

tr: vt. 使傾覆, (重量、價值)超過, 使失去均衡, 跌倒
vi. 失去平衡
n. 超重, 超量, 失去平衡
def: v. cause to be off balance

tr: vt. 威壓, 壓服, 壓抑
vi. 結果實過多, 繁殖過度
def: v. overcome
v. bear too much

tr: a. 傲慢的, 驕傲自大的, 蠻橫的, 壓倒一切的
[法] 自大的, 專制的, 壓倒的
def: v overcome
v bear too much
v contract the abdominal muscles during childbirth to ease delivery

tr: a. 停息的, 盛開過的, 浮誇的
overblow的過去分詞
def: s. past the stage of full bloom

tr: a. 陰天的, 陰暗的, 愁悶的
陰天的；烏雲密佈的
def: n. a long whipstitch or overhand stitch overlying an edge to prevent raveling
n. a cast that falls beyond the intended spot
v. make overcast or cloudy

ex.en: The sky was overcast when we left for school.
ex.zh: 我們出門上學時，天空陰雲密佈。

ex.en: Although overcast conditions reduce solar electricity generation, modern panels can still produce useful amounts of power.
ex.zh: 雖然陰天會降低太陽能發電量，但現代太陽能板仍能產生可供使用的電力。

col: an overcast sky｜陰雲密佈的天空
words.tip: 指天空被雲層覆蓋，不一定下雨。

tr: a. 過於自信的, 自負的
[法] 過於自信的, 過於自恃的
def: s marked by excessive confidence

tr: vt. 容納過多的人, 使過度擁擠
def: v. cause to crowd together too much
v. crowd together too much

tr: vt. 透支(銀行帳戶), 把(弓等)拉得過度, 誇大, 誇張
vi. 透支
def: v. draw more money from than is available

tr: a. 過期的, 未兌的, 遲到的, 早就成熟的
[經] 過期未付的
逾期的；延誤的
早該發生的
def: s past due; not paid at the scheduled time
Not paid, returned, or completed by the expected time.
Needed or deserved much earlier than now.

ex.en: I found an overdue library book under my bed.
ex.zh: 我在床底下發現了一本逾期未還的圖書館藏書。

ex.en: Investment in rural public transport is long overdue, as many residents still lack reliable services.
ex.zh: 農村公共交通早就該得到投資，因為許多居民至今仍缺乏可靠的交通服務。

col: an overdue library book｜逾期未還的圖書館書籍
words.tip: long overdue強調“早就該有或該做”，不只是遲到。

tr: v. 過分強調
def: v. place special or excessive emphasis on

tr: vt. 評價過高, 過高估價
n. 估計過高, 評價過高
def: n. an appraisal that is too high
n. a calculation that results in an estimate that is too high
v. make too high an estimate of

tr: n. 溢值, 超值, 氾濫
v. (使)氾濫, (使)溢出, (使)充溢
[計] 上溢; 溢出
溢出；滿溢
充滿；擠滿
def: n. the occurrence of surplus liquid (as water) exceeding the limit or capacity
v. flow or run over (a limit or brim)
To flow over the edge because a container is too full.

ex.en: The bath overflowed while I was answering the door.
ex.zh: 我去應門時，浴缸裡的水溢了出來。

ex.en: During heavy rainfall, urban drains may overflow and carry polluted water into nearby rivers.
ex.zh: 暴雨期間，城市排水管道可能滿溢，將汙水帶入附近河流。

words.tip: 動詞重音在末音節，名詞重音在首音節。

tr: vt. 分解檢查, 翻修, 精細檢查, 徹底革新

部分重疊；有共同之處
def: n. a representation of common ground between theories or phenomena
n. the property of partial coincidence in time
v. coincide partially or wholly

ex.en: The curtains overlap slightly in the middle of the window.
ex.zh: 窗簾在窗戶中間略有重疊。

ex.en: University courses often overlap in content, allowing students to explore connections between different academic disciplines.
ex.zh: 大學課程的內容常有重疊，使學生能夠探索不同學科之間的聯繫。

words.tip: 動詞重音在後，名詞在前；過去式overlapped。

tr: vt. 超載, 過載, 超過負荷
n. 超載, 負荷過多
使超載；使負擔過重
使電路過載

n. an excessive burden
v. become overloaded

ex.en: Don't overload your backpack with things you won't use.
ex.zh: 別把用不上的東西塞進背包，讓它變得太重。

ex.en: Schools should avoid overloading students with homework, as excessive pressure can undermine motivation and wellbeing.
ex.zh: 學校應避免讓學生承擔過重的作業負擔，因為過度的壓力會削弱學習動力並損害身心健康。

tr: vt. 俯瞰, 遠眺, 沒注意到

忽略；未注意到
俯瞰；面向
寬容；不追究

v. look past, fail to notice
v. watch over

ex.en: I overlooked a small crack in the bowl.
ex.zh: 我沒注意到碗上有一道小裂紋。

ex.en: Urban planners sometimes overlook the needs of older residents when designing new public transport systems.
ex.zh: 城市規劃者在設計新的公共交通系統時，有時會忽略老年居民的需求。

col: overlook the fact that｜忽略這一事實
words.tip: overlook可指忽略或俯瞰；不要與監督的oversee混淆。

def: n. a manually operated device to correct the operation of an automatic device
v. prevail over
v. counteract the normal operation of (an automatic gear shift in a vehicle)

tr: [醫] [骨折端]重迭, 架迭

tr: vt. 統治, 威壓, 打敗, 駁回
[法] 否決, 駁回, 批駁
否決；駁回
def: v. rule against
To use authority to reject or reverse a decision or objection.

ex.en: The manager overruled my request to close the shop early.
ex.zh: 經理否決了我提前關店的請求。

ex.en: National authorities may overrule local planning decisions when major infrastructure projects serve the wider public interest.
ex.zh: 當重大基礎設施項目符合更廣泛的公共利益時，國家主管部門可能否決地方規劃決定。

words.tip: 強調憑更高權力否決，不只是表示不同意。

tr: vt. 向下看, 瞭望, 監督, 偷看到
[法] 監察, 監督, 俯瞰

[經] 監督權
疏忽；遺漏
監督；監管
def: n. an unintentional omission resulting from failure to notice something
n. a mistake resulting from inattention
A mistake caused by failing to notice or consider something.

ex.en: Through an oversight, I left your lunch at home.
ex.zh: 由於一時疏忽，我把你的午餐落在家裡了。

ex.en: Independent oversight of public spending can reduce corruption and strengthen citizens' confidence in government institutions.
ex.zh: 對公共支出進行獨立監督可以減少腐敗，並增強公民對政府機構的信任。

col: an unfortunate oversight｜令人遺憾的疏忽
words.tip: 作“疏忽”通常可數；作“監督”通常不可數。

tr: vt. 誇大的敘述, 誇張, 過分強調

tr: vt. 課稅過重, 使負擔過度

tr: n. 推翻, 瓦解, 傾覆

推翻；顛覆
推翻；政權覆滅
def: n. the termination of a ruler or institution (especially by force)
v. cause the downfall of; of rulers
to remove a ruler or government from power

ex.en: The film follows citizens who overthrow an unfair ruler.
ex.zh: 這部電影講述民眾推翻不公正統治者的故事。

ex.en: Economic hardship can weaken public support for a government and encourage attempts to overthrow it.
ex.zh: 經濟困難可能削弱公眾對政府的支持，並促使人們嘗試推翻它。

col: the overthrow of a ruler｜統治者被推翻
words.tip: 過去式overthrew，過去分詞overthrown。

tr: vt.使過度疲勞
def: v. tire excessively

tr: n. 主動表示, 事件的開端, 序言, 提議, 提案, 初步交涉

使不知所措；使情緒難抑
使不堪重負
壓倒；徹底擊敗
def: v. overcome, as with emotions or perceptual stimuli
v. charge someone with too many tasks
To affect someone so strongly they cannot cope.

ex.en: I felt overwhelmed by everyone's kindness after the move.
ex.zh: 搬家後，大家的善意讓我感動得不知如何是好。

ex.en: A sudden increase in visitors can overwhelm local infrastructure unless tourism growth is carefully managed.
ex.zh: 如果不謹慎管理旅遊業增長，遊客驟增可能使當地基礎設施不堪重負。

col: be overwhelmed by emotion｜情緒激動得難以自持
overwhelm local services｜使當地服務不堪重負
words.tip: 人感到 overwhelmed；事物令人 overwhelming。

tr: a. 過分勞累的, 過度緊張的, 神經質的, 過度興奮的, 過分推敲的, 不自然的

To react with oxygen, or lose electrons in a chemical reaction.

ex.en: The cut apple began to oxidize and turn brown.
ex.zh: 切開的蘋果開始氧化，變成了褐色。

ex.en: When exposed to air and moisture, iron can oxidize, weakening structures unless protective coatings are applied.
ex.zh: 鐵暴露於空氣和水分中時會氧化，若不塗覆保護層，就可能削弱結構的強度。

col: oxidize in air｜在空氣中氧化
words.tip: 英式也拼作oxidise；氧化不一定涉及氧氣。

極其細緻的；煞費苦心的

Done with great care, effort, and attention to detail.

ex.en: She made painstaking repairs to her grandmother's old quilt.
ex.zh: 她極其細緻地修補了祖母的舊被子。

ex.en: The preservation of historic buildings requires painstaking research into original materials and traditional construction methods.
ex.zh: 保護歷史建築需要對原有材料和傳統建造方法進行細緻深入的研究。

col: painstaking attention to detail｜對細節的極度關注
words.tip: 是形容詞，強調費心且細緻，不只是辛苦。

可接受的

pleasant enough to eat or drink
acceptable or satisfactory, even if not entirely welcome

ex.en: A little lemon juice made the soup more palatable.
ex.zh: 加了一點檸檬汁後，湯變得更合口味了。

ex.en: Gradual increases in public transport fares may be more palatable to passengers than sudden price rises.
ex.zh: 與突然漲價相比，逐步提高公共交通票價可能更容易讓乘客接受。

col: make something palatable｜使某物可接受
words.tip: 不一定指“美味極了”；也可形容方案可接受。

To give someone special care, comfort, or excessive attention

ex.en: I pamper myself with a warm bath on Sundays.
ex.zh: 每到星期天，我都會泡個熱水澡犒勞自己。

ex.en: Parents who constantly pamper their children may unintentionally limit opportunities for them to develop independence.
ex.zh: 總是嬌慣孩子的父母可能會無意中限制孩子培養獨立性的機會。

col: pamper someone with gifts｜用禮物寵愛某人
words.tip: 不一定含貶義；pamper yourself常指犒勞自己。

n. shallow container made of metal

ex.en: Heat the oil in a pan before adding onions.
ex.zh: 先把鍋裡的油燒熱，再放入洋蔥。

ex.en: Television chefs can encourage healthier eating by demonstrating how to prepare nutritious meals using a single pan.
ex.zh: 電視廚師可以通過演示如何用一口鍋烹製營養餐，來鼓勵更健康的飲食。

col: be panned by critics｜受到評論家的嚴厲批評
pan across a scene｜搖攝整個場景
words.tip: 作動詞時過去式為panned，現在分詞為panning。

tr: n. 萬能藥, 靈丹妙藥

萬能藥；萬全之策

n. hypothetical remedy for all ills or diseases; once sought by the alchemists
Something believed to solve every problem or cure every illness.

ex.en: A new phone is no panacea for your troubles.
ex.zh: 換部新手機並不能解決你所有的煩惱。

ex.en: Although technology can improve classroom learning, it should not be regarded as a panacea for educational inequality.
ex.zh: 雖然技術可以改善課堂學習，但不應被視為解決教育不平等的萬全之策。

col: a panacea for｜解決……的萬能之策
a universal panacea｜包治百病的靈丹妙藥
words.tip: 常用a panacea for；多用於否定萬能解法。

恐慌；驚慌

n. sudden mass fear and anxiety over anticipated events
v. be overcome by a sudden fear

ex.en: I felt a moment of panic when my keys disappeared.
ex.zh: 發現鑰匙不見時，我一時驚慌起來。

ex.en: Clear communication during emergencies can reduce public panic and help people follow safety instructions more effectively.
ex.zh: 緊急情況下清晰的溝通能減少公眾恐慌，幫助人們更有效地遵循安全指示。

showing a wide view of a large surrounding area

ex.en: Our balcony offers panoramic views of the harbour.
ex.zh: 從我們的陽臺可以俯瞰港口全景。

ex.en: Hotels with panoramic coastal views can attract tourists while increasing pressure on sensitive marine environments.
ex.zh: 擁有海岸全景的酒店能吸引遊客，但也會增加脆弱海洋環境承受的壓力。

words.tip: 常修飾view，強調能看到廣闊的周圍景色。

tr: n. 手勢, 啞劇, 舞劇
v. 打手勢, 演啞劇

v act out without words but with gestures and bodily movements only

def: n. (logic) a statement that contradicts itself
A statement or situation that seems contradictory but may be true.

ex.en: It seems a paradox that resting helps me accomplish more.
ex.zh: 休息反而能讓我完成更多事情，這似乎很矛盾。

ex.en: Modern technology creates a paradox: people can communicate instantly yet still experience deep social isolation.
ex.zh: 現代技術帶來一種看似矛盾的現象：人們能即時交流，卻仍感到深深的社會孤立。

col: present a paradox｜呈現看似矛盾的情況
words.tip: 強調看似矛盾卻可能成立，不等於普通錯誤。

ex.en: Some spinal injuries can paralyze both of a person's legs.
ex.zh: 某些脊柱損傷會導致雙腿癱瘓。

ex.en: Severe flooding can paralyze urban transport networks, preventing workers from reaching essential services and workplaces.
ex.zh: 嚴重洪災會使城市交通網絡癱瘓，導致勞動者無法前往基本服務場所和工作地點。

col: paralyzed by fear｜嚇得無法動彈
words.tip: 美式拼寫paralyze；英式通常寫paralyse。

a. 最重要的, 最高的, 至上的
首要的；至關重要的
def: s having superior power and influence

tr: n. 有權的人, 有勢力的人, 統治者
